+   A elements lie in better bins, A < K ≤ A + c_B.
+3. If c_B > 64 (a dense bin; ties), refine: the better bins become selected,
+   the worse ones dead, and the live ones get new digits from their keys
+   ((kmax - key) >> s, s so that the live key range fits 2048 bins), or from
+   their positions once the keys are all equal. Repeat.
+4. c_B ≤ 64: collect the bin's elements into an LDS list; wave 0 ranks them
+   (64-bit composite key, position ascending on ties) while the other waves
+   write the output.
+5. Output: the elements better than B in position order (a packed block scan
+   of per-thread counts gives every one its slot), then the bin's winners at
+   A + rank. The copy-out maps each local position through the block-table
+   row (prefetched into LDS): tk[row·512 + i] = bt[loc >> bs_log2]·bs + loc %
+   bs, -1 past the count; out_local[row][i] = loc, -1 past it (vLLM's top-k
+   buffer); tk_lens[row] = valid ? count : 0.
+
+Element state d (a byte offset into the histogram, so ds_add needs no
+address math): selected 4·lane, live 4·(64 + digit), dead 4·(2113 + lane).
+Selected / dead are spread over the lanes: 64 lanes adding to one LDS word
+cost 128 clk per instruction (measured), and a row's dead tail (positions
+≥ n) is up to 2k elements.
+
+Kernargs: see KA. Grid = rows, block = T.
+"""
+
+import regex as re
+
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.asm.kernels.kmod import KArgs, kernel_source
+
+K = 512
+PFLAG = "nt"  # the merge's poll loads: skip vL1, read the XCD's L2 (a row's CTAs share an XCD; sc1 loads
+# miss the producers' plain stores while those sit dirty in L2)
+CAP = 64  # the collected bin's capacity (one wave ranks it)
+DIG0 = 64  # live digit d sits at 4·(DIG0 + d)
+DEAD0 = DIG0 + 2049  # dead states 4·(DEAD0 + lane)
+
+KA = KArgs(
+    ("logits", "ptr"),
+    ("lens", "ptr"),
+    ("valid", "ptr"),
+    ("req", "ptr"),
+    ("bt", "ptr"),
+    ("out_local", "ptr"),
+    ("tk", "ptr"),
+    ("tk_lens", "ptr"),
+    ("lstride", "u32"),
+    ("bt_stride", "u32"),
+    ("local_stride", "u32"),
+    ("bs_log2", "u32"),
+)
+KA_DBG = KArgs(*KA.args, ("dbg", "ptr"))
+NSTAMP = 16
+
+# LDS map (bytes)
+HIST_OFF = 12  # state d counts at HIST_OFF + d: digit 1 at byte 272 (b128-aligned)
+HIST_END = 8736  # ≥ HIST_OFF + 4·(DEAD0 + 64), a multiple of 16
+RED_MM = HIST_END  # 16 × 8: max / min
+RED_S1 = RED_MM + 128  # 16 × 8 dwords: scans
+RED_S2 = RED_S1 + 512
+RES = RED_S2 + 512  # B4, A, c_B
+CNT = RES + 16  # collect counter
+RED_K = CNT + 16  # 2 × 16 × 8: slow-path key / position max, min
+CAND = RED_K + 256  # CAP × (value, position)
+OUT = CAND + 8 * CAP  # K local positions in output order, then 64 dummy slots
+BT = OUT + 4 * (K + 64)  # the block-table row
+assert HIST_END >= HIST_OFF + 4 * (DEAD0 + 64) and HIST_END % 16 == 0 and CAND % 8 == 0
+
+
+def source(
+    nw: int = 8,
+    nl: int = 5,
+    name: str | None = None,
+    bt_max: int = 1024,
+    stamps: bool = False,
+    row: str = "s2",
+    lg_lds: int | None = None,
+    lg_sel: str | None = None,
+    lg_flag: str = "",
+    body_only: bool = False,
+    pre: bool = False,
+    pfx: str = "",
+    cand_out: bool = False,
+    cand_in: str | None = None,
+    bt_n: str | None = None,
+    bt_off: int = BT,
+    exit_to: str | None = None,
+    filt: bool = False,
+    caps: int = 0,
+    fallback: str = "",
+    cand_range: str | None = None,
+    xstamp=None,
+    st_flag: str = "",
+    tag: str = "",
+    front: dict | None = None,
+    pos_lds: int | None = None,
+    tau_slot: bool = False,
+    k: int = K,
+    blk_out: bool = False,
+    remap: int | None = None,
+):
+    """stamps: wave 0 writes s_memtime at the phase boundaries to dbg[row][0..15] (u64), for profiling.
+    For embedding (idx_logits.py): row = the SGPR holding the row (kept intact); lg_lds = the LDS byte offset
+    of the row's logits (element e at lg_lds + 4e), used when lg_sel (an SGPR) is 0 or always if lg_sel is
+    None; lg_flag = cache flag of the global logits loads (e.g. "nt"); body_only: return the code lines (they
+    end the program) instead of a kernel; pre: the caller has loaded the kernargs into s[4:23] and n, req and
+    the valid word into s25, s26, s27.
+    Two-level top-k (idx_logits wide rows): pfx makes the labels unique (two bodies in one kernel); exit_to:
+    branch there instead of s_endpgm. cand_out: no block table; the copy-out writes the selected elements'
+    values (from LDS lg_lds) to s[14:15] + 4i and their positions s22 + e to s[16:17] + 4i, i < min(n, K).
+    cand_in = an SGPR pair holding a candidates row: 8 B slots (value, position | tag << 24), polled with sc1
+    loads until every slot < cand_range carries s[tag] (= tag << 24): the producers store them without a
+    release; slots holding NaN are dead, and n (s25) is the row's real n (count and n ≤ K logic). The
+    positions stay in VGPRs; ties at the cut are ranked by them, so the slots may come in any order.
+    bt_n = the SGPR with the row's real n (for the block-table row, else n); bt_off = the block-table row's
+    LDS offset.
+    caps (with cand_out): the output is a segment of caps slots at s[14:15] + 8 i, (value, position | s[tag])
+    for i < count as above, the rest (NaN, 0xffffff | s[tag]) (the merge reads every segment: NaN = no
+    element). cand_range (with cand_in) = an SGPR with the number of slots to read.
+    tau_slot (cand_out): wave 0 also stores (τ key, tag) at s[16:17] (τ = the filter's, 0 for the exact body).
+    front = dict(nseg=SGPR with S, cmax, clds, to_c, to_b) (with cand_in): only the merge's front end: poll the S
+    τ slots (cand_in + 8 (range + s)) until all carry the tag, τ_row = their max (a lower bound of the row's
+    K-th key), poll the candidates, compact the live ones with key ≥ τ_row into LDS (values at clds, positions
+    at clds + 4 cmax), n (s25) = their count; → to_c if n ≤ cmax, else to_b (the full merge, which re-polls).
+    pos_lds (with lg_lds): the elements' positions are at pos_lds + 4e (a compacted candidate list).
+    xstamp(p, emit): emits the embedding kernel's stamp p (through emit) at the filter's phase boundaries.
+    k: the top-k's K (the plain path; filt / cand_in / front stay at K = 512). blk_out: the copy-out only writes
+    the positions to out_local[row][i] (-1 past the count): no block table, tk or tk_lens (the candidate
+    source's top-2048 blocks, its row = the block scores, n = the block count); the bt_stride kernarg = the live
+    rows: rows past it (graph padding) output -1 only (their stale or zero scores: an all-equal row is the radix
+    select's worst case, every ds_add on one LDS word).
+    filt (needs cand_out, caps, lg_lds): no exact top-K; the caller has filled the histogram (digit
+    2048 - (key >> 21) per live element, below); the threshold bin of that and, if more than caps elements
+    are at or above it, of a second level (digit 2048 - ((key >> 10) & 2047) inside it) gives a key τ with
+    K ≤ #{key ≥ τ} ≤ caps; those elements are the candidates. More than caps at both levels (ties) →
+    branch to `fallback` (the exact body)."""
+    T = 64 * nw
+    EPT = 4 * nl
+    KT = k  # (k is a loop variable below)
+    assert remap is None or cand_out
+    # remap (cand_out; idx_logits gather): element e's position = 8 · LDS[remap + 16 (e >> 3)] + (e & 7) (the
+    # slice's block table) instead of s22 + e
+    assert KT == K or not (filt or cand_in or front or cand_out), KT
+    assert not blk_out or not (cand_out or cand_in or front or filt)
+    out_end = OUT + 4 * (KT + 64)  # OUT: k positions, then 64 dummy slots
+    bt_off = max(bt_off, out_end) if bt_off == BT else bt_off
+    assert nw in (4, 8, 16), nw
+    G = 2048 // T  # bins per thread in the scan
+    name = name or (
+        f"idx_topk_w{nw}_l{nl}"
+        + (f"_k{KT}" if KT != K else "")
+        + ("_blk" if blk_out else "")
+        + ("_dbg" if stamps else "")
+    )
+    ka = KA_DBG if stamps else KA
+    lds = (
+        BT
+        if cand_out
+        else max(out_end, BT)
+        if blk_out
+        else max(BT, bt_off + 4 * bt_max)
+    )
+    assert not filt or (cand_out and lg_lds is not None and caps and fallback)
+    assert not cand_out or (caps >= K and tag)
+    assert not cand_in or (tag and cand_range)
+    assert not front or cand_in
+    FB = (
+        10 if KT < 1024 else 12
+    )  # packed output counts: fields of FB bits (a load's count ≤ k)
+    FPD = 32 // FB
+    NQ = -(-nl // FPD)
+    assert nl <= 18 and NQ <= 6 and KT < 4096
+
+    # ---- registers: v0 tid, v1 lane, v2 4·tid, v3 one, v4 zero, v5 16·tid, v6 nan, v7 dead state, v8 4·tid,
+    # v9 selected state, v10 OUT dummy slot, v12..15 zeros / stamp temps; VAL, ST, then temps
+    VAL = 16
+    ST = VAL + EPT
+    POS = ST + EPT  # cand_in / pos_lds: the elements' positions
+    has_pos = bool(cand_in) or pos_lds is not None
+    TMP = POS + (EPT if has_pos and not front else 0)
+    t = [TMP + i for i in range(48)]
+    nv = TMP + 48
+    c = []
+    A = c.append
+    lbl = [0]
+
+    def L(p="L"):
+        lbl[0] += 1
+        return f".{p}{lbl[0]}"
+
+    def nop(n=1):
+        A(f"  s_nop {n}")
+
+    # SGPRs: s[4:19] 8 pointers, s20 lstride, s21 bt_stride, s22 local_stride, s23 bs_log2,
+    # s24 row·4, s25 n, s26 req, s27 valid word, s28 wave, s[32:35] logits rsrc, s[36:39] bt rsrc,
+    # s40 B4, s41 A (this round), s42 c_B, s43 need, s44 A total, s45 / s46 reduction results, s47 cnt,
+    # s48.. temps, s[64:71] stamps
+    S_N, S_REQ, S_W = 25, 26, 28
+    S_B4, S_A, S_CB, S_NEED, S_AT, S_CNT = 40, 41, 42, 43, 44, 47
+
+    nst = [0]
+
+    def stamp(early: bool = False):
+        """s_memtime → dbg[row][p] from wave 0 lane 0 (waits for this wave's LDS / scalar ops); early: the
+        time taken at kernel entry."""
+        if not stamps:
+            return
+        p = nst[0]
+        nst[0] += 1
+        assert p < NSTAMP
+        skip = L("Lst")
+        if early:
+            A("  s_mov_b64 s[64:65], s[70:71]")
+        else:
+            A("  s_memtime s[64:65]")
+        A("  s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0)")
+        A("  s_cmp_eq_u32 s28, 0")
+        A(f"  s_cbranch_scc0 {skip}")
+        A("  s_mov_b64 s[68:69], exec")
+        A("  s_mov_b64 exec, 1")
+        A("  v_mov_b32 v12, s64")
+        A("  v_mov_b32 v13, s65")
+        A(f"  v_mov_b32 v14, {8 * p}")
+        A("  global_store_dwordx2 v14, v[12:13], s[66:67]")
+        A("  s_mov_b64 exec, s[68:69]")
+        A(f"{skip}:")
+
+    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
+    def wave_reduce(ops, regs, tmps, steps=6):
+        """ops[i] (e.g. max_f32) over the lanes of regs[i]; every lane gets the result (fixed order). steps < 6:
+        only the first ones (e.g. 3 = within 8 consecutive lanes)."""
+        ctls = ("quad_perm:[1,0,3,2]", "quad_perm:[2,3,0,1]", "row_ror:4", "row_ror:8")
+        for ctl in ctls[:steps]:
+            for r, tp in zip(regs, tmps):
+                A(f"  v_mov_b32 v{tp}, v{r}")
+            nop(1)
+            for op, r, tp in zip(ops, regs, tmps):
+                A(f"  v_{op}_dpp v{r}, v{tp}, v{r} {ctl} row_mask:0xf bank_mask:0xf")
+        for sw in ("v_permlane32_swap_b32", "v_permlane16_swap_b32")[
+            : max(0, steps - 4)
+        ]:
+            for r, tp in zip(regs, tmps):
+                A(f"  v_mov_b32 v{tp}, v{r}")
+            nop(1)
+            for r, tp in zip(regs, tmps):
+                A(f"  {sw} v{r}, v{tp}")
+            nop(4)
+            for op, r, tp in zip(ops, regs, tmps):
+                A(f"  v_{op} v{r}, v{r}, v{tp}")
+
+    def wave_scan(regs):
+        """Inclusive u32 scan over the 64 lanes (lane order)."""
+        for ctl in (
+            "row_shr:1 row_mask:0xf bank_mask:0xf bound_ctrl:0",
+            "row_shr:2 row_mask:0xf bank_mask:0xf bound_ctrl:0",
+            "row_shr:4 row_mask:0xf bank_mask:0xf bound_ctrl:0",
+            "row_shr:8 row_mask:0xf bank_mask:0xf bound_ctrl:0",
+            "row_bcast:15 row_mask:0xa bank_mask:0xf",
+            "row_bcast:31 row_mask:0xc bank_mask:0xf",
+        ):
+            nop(1)
+            for r in regs:
+                A(f"  v_add_u32_dpp v{r}, v{r}, v{r} {ctl}")
+        nop(1)
+
+    def block_scan(regs, red, tmps, totals):
+        """Inclusive u32 scan over the T threads (tid order) of each reg; totals[i] (SGPR) gets reg i's block
+        total. tmps: 2·len(regs) VGPRs. Uses LDS red[0 : 4·len(regs)·NW]; has one barrier."""
+        n = len(regs)
+        wave_scan(regs)
+        A("  s_lshl_b64 s[50:51], 1, 63")
+        A("  s_mov_b64 exec, s[50:51]")
+        A(f"  v_mov_b32 v{t[47]}, s{S_W}")
+        A(f"  v_mul_u32_u24 v{t[47]}, {4 * n}, v{t[47]}")
+        for i, r in enumerate(regs):
+            A(f"  ds_write_b32 v{t[47]}, v{r} offset:{red + 4 * i}")
+        A("  s_mov_b64 exec, -1")
+        A("  s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0)")
+        A("  s_barrier")
+        A(f"  v_mul_u32_u24 v{t[47]}, {4 * n}, v1")
+        A(f"  v_cmp_gt_u32 vcc, {nw}, v1")
+        for i in range(n):
+            A(f"  v_mov_b32 v{tmps[i]}, 0")
+        A("  s_and_saveexec_b64 s[50:51], vcc")
+        for i in range(n):
+            A(f"  ds_read_b32 v{tmps[i]}, v{t[47]} offset:{red + 4 * i}")
+        A("  s_mov_b64 exec, s[50:51]")
+        A("  s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0)")
+        for i in range(n):
+            A(f"  v_mov_b32 v{tmps[n + i]}, v{tmps[i]}")
+        wave_scan(tmps[:n])
+        for i, r in enumerate(regs):
+            A(f"  v_readlane_b32 s52, v{tmps[i]}, s{S_W}")
+            A(f"  v_readlane_b32 s53, v{tmps[n + i]}, s{S_W}")
+            A(f"  v_readlane_b32 s{totals[i]}, v{tmps[i]}, {nw - 1}")
+            A("  s_sub_u32 s52, s52, s53")
+            A(f"  v_add_u32 v{r}, s52, v{r}")
+
+    def cross_wave(ops, regs, region, tmps):
+        """Regs (already wave-reduced, uniform per wave) → block result in every lane: wave w's value at
+        region + 8 w (+4), then a reduce over the NW values (replicated mod NW across the lanes)."""
+        A(f"  v_mov_b32 v{t[44]}, s{S_W}")
+        A(f"  v_lshlrev_b32 v{t[44]}, 3, v{t[44]}")
+        A("  s_mov_b64 exec, 1")
+        for i, r in enumerate(regs):
+            A(f"  ds_write_b32 v{t[44]}, v{r} offset:{region + 4 * i}")
+        A("  s_mov_b64 exec, -1")
+        A("  s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0)")
+        A("  s_barrier")
+        A(f"  v_and_b32 v{t[44]}, {nw - 1}, v1")
+        A(f"  v_lshlrev_b32 v{t[44]}, 3, v{t[44]}")
+        for i, r in enumerate(regs):
+            A(f"  ds_read_b32 v{r}, v{t[44]} offset:{region + 4 * i}")
+        A("  s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0)")
+        wave_reduce(ops, regs, tmps, steps=nw.bit_length() - 1)
+
+    def remap_pos(r, tmp):
+        """v[r] = element e → its position through the remap table (waits for the LDS)."""
+        A(f"  v_lshrrev_b32 v{tmp}, 3, v{r}")
+        A(f"  v_lshlrev_b32 v{tmp}, 4, v{tmp}")
+        A(f"  v_add_u32 v{tmp}, {remap}, v{tmp}")
+        A(f"  ds_read_b32 v{tmp}, v{tmp}")
+        A("  s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0)")
+        A(f"  v_and_b32 v{r}, 7, v{r}")
+        A(f"  v_lshl_or_b32 v{r}, v{tmp}, 3, v{r}")
+
+    def pos_of(k, j, dst):
+        if has_pos:
+            A(f"  v_and_b32 v{dst}, 0xffffff, v{POS + 4 * k + j}")
+        else:
+            A(f"  v_add_u32 v{dst}, {4 * k * T + j}, v2")
+
+    real_pos = pos_of
+
+    def key_of(v, dst, tmp):
+        """Dst ← orderable u32 key of the f32 in v."""
+        A(f"  v_ashrrev_i32 v{tmp}, 31, v{v}")
+        A(f"  v_or_b32 v{tmp}, 0x80000000, v{tmp}")
+        A(f"  v_xor_b32 v{dst}, v{tmp}, v{v}")
+
+    def zero_hist():
+        for r in range(12, 16):
+            A(f"  v_mov_b32 v{r}, 0")
+        for r in range(-(-HIST_END // (16 * T))):
+            lo = 16 * T * r
+            if lo + 16 * T <= HIST_END:
+                A(f"  ds_write_b128 v5, v[12:15] offset:{lo}")
+            else:
+                A(f"  v_cmp_gt_u32 vcc, {(HIST_END - lo) // 16}, v0")
+                A("  s_and_saveexec_b64 s[50:51], vcc")
+                A(f"  ds_write_b128 v5, v[12:15] offset:{lo}")
+                A("  s_mov_b64 exec, s[50:51]")
+
+    def histogram():
+        for i in range(EPT):
+            A(f"  ds_add_u32 v{ST + i}, v3 offset:{HIST_OFF}")
+        A("  s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0)")
+        A("  s_barrier")
+
+    def find_bin():
+        """Digits 1..2048 → the threshold bin for s[need]: S_B4 = its state value, S_A = count in better bins,
+        S_CB = c_B."""
+        h = t[0:G]
+        base = HIST_OFF + 4 * (DIG0 + 1)
+        A(f"  v_lshlrev_b32 v{t[40]}, {2 + (G.bit_length() - 1)}, v0")
+        if G >= 4:
+            for q in range(G // 4):
+                A(
+                    f"  ds_read_b128 v[{h[4 * q]}:{h[4 * q] + 3}], v{t[40]} offset:{base + 16 * q}"
+                )
+        else:
+            A(f"  ds_read_b64 v[{h[0]}:{h[1]}], v{t[40]} offset:{base}")
+        A("  s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0)")
+        ct = t[8]
+        A(f"  v_add_u32 v{ct}, v{h[0]}, v{h[1]}")
+        for g in range(2, G):
+            A(f"  v_add_u32 v{ct}, v{ct}, v{h[g]}")
+        A(f"  v_mov_b32 v{t[9]}, v{ct}")
+        block_scan([ct], RED_S1, [t[10], t[11]], [54])
+        cum, bB, bA, bC = t[12], t[13], t[14], t[15]
+        A(f"  v_sub_u32 v{cum}, v{ct}, v{t[9]}")
+        A(f"  v_mov_b32 v{bB}, 0")
+        A(f"  v_lshlrev_b32 v{t[17]}, {G.bit_length() - 1}, v0")
+        for g in range(G):
+            A(f"  v_add_u32 v{t[16]}, v{cum}, v{h[g]}")
+            A(f"  v_cmp_gt_u32 s[56:57], s{S_NEED}, v{cum}")  # cum < need
+            A(f"  v_cmp_le_u32 s[58:59], s{S_NEED}, v{t[16]}")  # need ≤ cum + h
+            A("  s_and_b64 s[56:57], s[56:57], s[58:59]")
+            A(f"  v_add_u32 v{t[18]}, {1 + g}, v{t[17]}")
+            A(f"  v_cndmask_b32_e64 v{bB}, v{bB}, v{t[18]}, s[56:57]")
+            A(f"  v_cndmask_b32_e64 v{bA}, v{bA}, v{cum}, s[56:57]")
+            A(f"  v_cndmask_b32_e64 v{bC}, v{bC}, v{h[g]}, s[56:57]")
+            A(f"  v_mov_b32 v{cum}, v{t[16]}")
+        A(f"  v_cmp_ne_u32 vcc, 0, v{bB}")
+        A("  s_and_saveexec_b64 s[50:51], vcc")
+        A(f"  v_add_lshl_u32 v{bB}, v{bB}, {DIG0}, 2")
+        A(f"  ds_write_b32 v4, v{bB} offset:{RES}")
+        A(f"  ds_write_b32 v4, v{bA} offset:{RES + 4}")
+        A(f"  ds_write_b32 v4, v{bC} offset:{RES + 8}")
+        A("  s_mov_b64 exec, s[50:51]")
+        A("  s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0)")
+        A("  s_barrier")
+        A(f"  ds_read_b32 v{t[20]}, v4 offset:{RES}")
+        A(f"  ds_read_b32 v{t[21]}, v4 offset:{RES + 4}")
+        A(f"  ds_read_b32 v{t[22]}, v4 offset:{RES + 8}")
+        A("  s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0)")
+        A(f"  v_readfirstlane_b32 s{S_B4}, v{t[20]}")
+        A(f"  v_readfirstlane_b32 s{S_A}, v{t[21]}")

+"""K2 skeleton: the FFN half as one persistent kernel,
+256 CTAs × 256 threads, the step-3 phase kernels as bodies separated by grid
+barriers.
+
+- **Bodies:** each phase kernel's code, unchanged except that labels get the
+  phase tag, ``s_endpgm`` branches to the phase exit and every store gets
+  ``sc1`` (a barrier doesn't publish plain stores across XCDs). Before a body
+  the skeleton points s[0:1] at that phase's block of the combined kernargs
+  (laid out exactly as the phase's own KArgs), sets s2 = CTA index and v0 =
+  thread id, EXEC = all. Phases with fewer CTAs skip the rest; the combine
+  (grid 2.5 M) loops over virtual CTAs b, b + 256, ...
+- **Reserved:** s96 barrier index (leader wave), s97 CTA, s[98:99] kernarg
+  base, s100-s101 virtual-CTA loop, v255 thread id. Bodies use ≤ s95, ≤ v247.
+- **Grid barrier** (common/pk_barrier.py's hierarchical one): all waves wait
+  for their stores and ``s_barrier``; wave 0 adds to its XCD group's counter
+  (CTA b runs on XCD b % 8); the group's last arriver adds to the global
+  counter; the last global arriver writes the barrier index to the 8 release
+  lines (sc1); wave 0 polls its group's line, then ``s_barrier``.
+- **Coherence** (``coh``): "plain" (default): plain loads, sc1
+  stores, nothing invalidated. Coherent because (a) the dispatch acquire
+  invalidates every XCD's L2 at kernel start (the chain relies on the same),
+  (b) every scratch buffer is written in one phase and only read in later
+  ones, so no XCD can hold a line of it from before the write, and (c) sc1
+  stores write through to memory. Only the barrier words are read before
+  they are written; they keep their sc1 polls. Bitwise equal to the chain on
+  layers 3/5/22/30, M 64-256, 5 launches each; stage 1's slowest CTA 8 µs
+  faster than with "loads" at M 256.
+  "loads": loads of data written earlier
+  in the launch (SC1_LOADS: per body, the buffer-resource / base SGPRs) get
+  ``sc1``, and moe_ug1 / moe_down1 read ``counts`` with a vector sc1 load;
+  nothing is invalidated, so code, weights and inputs keep their L2 lines.
+  "inv": plain loads, ``buffer_inv sc1`` after each release (first version:
+  ~1.5 µs per barrier). "sc0": timing experiment only.
+  No ``s_dcache_inv``: it made every phase's kernarg s_loads miss (~2 µs per
+  phase). The only scalar load of data written in the kernel is moe_ug1 /
+  moe_down1 reading ``counts``, which nothing reads before P4 writes it, and
+  the kernel-start acquire clears the scalar cache of earlier launches.
+- **No per-launch memset:** counters and release lines only grow. At start
+  wave 0 reads its release line, R0 = the last completed barrier; barrier k
+  waits for counters (R0 + k)·32 / ·8 and release value R0 + k (equality and
+  signed differences, so u32 wrap is fine). Every CTA reads R0 before it
+  arrives anywhere, so nothing races it. The buffer is zeroed once at
+  allocation (and must be re-zeroed after a timed-out launch).
+- **Timeline:** wave 0 stores s_memrealtime (100 MHz, low dword) per CTA:
+  slot 0 start, 2k-1 all waves done with phase k, 2k barrier k released,
+  2 NB + 1 end; slot 31 = 0x80000000 | k if barrier k timed out.
+- **Knock-outs:** bit i of ``knock`` skips body i (in BODIES order); the
+  barriers still run.
+"""
+
+import regex as re
+
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.asm.kernels import ffn_route as fr
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.asm.kernels import (
+    ffn_seam,
+    moe_combine,
+    moe_down1,
+    moe_prep,
+    moe_ug1,
+)
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.asm.kernels.kmod import KArgs, kernel_source
+
+NCU, GRP = 256, 8
+PER_GRP = NCU // GRP
+SPIN = 1 << 22
+TL_SLOTS = 32
+BAR_BYTES = 8192  # global counter @0, group g's counter @256 + 256 g, release line @4352 + 256 g
+SKEL = [("bar", "ptr"), ("tl", "ptr"), ("m", "u32"), ("knock", "u32")]
+OFF_BAR, OFF_TL, OFF_M, OFF_KNOCK = 0, 8, 16, 20

+# that point at data written earlier in the same launch

+    "fin": {32, 36},
+    "rt": {20},
+    "sgu": {28, 32},
+    "p3": {24, 44},
+    "prep": {28},
+    "ug": {32, 36, 78},
+    "dn": {32, 36, 40, 78},
+    "sdn": {28, 32},
+    "comb": {16, 20, 40},

+PLAIN_STORES = {"seam": {56}, "fin": {48, 52, 56}, "p3": {32}, "comb": {24}}
+
+
+def phases(layout: str = "base"):
+    """Phases in order; a barrier follows each but the last. Bodies within a
+    phase run back to back in each CTA. Grid: an int, "m" or "comb" (virtual
+    CTAs over all 256), or (virtual grid, first CTA, CTA count): CTAs first ..
+    first + count - 1 loop over virtual CTAs v, v + count, ...
+    layout: "base" or options joined by "+":

+    - "split": router on CTAs 0-127, shared gate_up on 128-255 (slower).
+    - "cost": P4 splits stage 2 by cost (moe_prep dsplit), stage 2 reads it.
+    - "pst" (source()): plain stores for PLAIN_STORES.
+    - "part": the combine adds the shared expert's output (moe_combine add):
+      ``out`` = bf16(routed + shared), the MoE's output before its all-reduce.
+    - "inv_ug" / "inv_dn" (source()): ``buffer_inv sc1`` after the barrier
+      before stage 1 / 2 and plain loads in that stage (coh "loads" only).
+    - "kpre" (source()): every wave loads the whole kernarg block once in the
+      prologue, so each body's kernarg s_loads hit the scalar cache."""
+    opts = set(layout.split("+")) - {"base"}
+    assert opts <= {
+        "sdn_prep",
+        "split",
+        "cost",
+        "inv_ug",
+        "inv_dn",
+        "part",
+        "pst",
+        "kpre",
+    }, layout
+    sdn = ("sdn", fr.source_shared_down(), fr.D_GRID)
+    p2 = (
+        [
+            ("rt", fr.source_router(), (fr.R_GRID, 0, 128)),
+            ("sgu", fr.source_shared(), (fr.S_GRID, 128, 128)),
+        ]
+        if "split" in opts
+        else [("rt", fr.source_router(), 256), ("sgu", fr.source_shared(), fr.S_GRID)]
+    )
+    cost = "cost" in opts
+    return [
+        [("seam", ffn_seam.source(), 256)],
+        [("fin", ffn_seam.source_fin(), "m")],
+        p2,
+        [("p3", fr.source_p3(), "m")],
+        [("prep", moe_prep.source(dsplit=cost), 1)]
+        + ([(sdn[0], sdn[1], (fr.D_GRID, 1, fr.D_GRID))] if "sdn_prep" in opts else []),
+        [("ug", moe_ug1.source(counts_vec=True), 256)],
+        [
+            (
+                "dn",
+                moe_down1.source(counts_vec=True, split="table" if cost else "ceil"),
+                256,
+            )
+        ]
+        + ([] if "sdn_prep" in opts else [sdn]),
+        [("comb", moe_combine.source(add="part" in opts), "comb")],
+    ]
+
+
+BODIES = [
+    tag for ph in phases() for tag, _, _ in ph
+]  # "base" order (knock bits follow the layout)
+NB = len(phases()) - 1
+
+
+def body_of(
+    k: dict, tag: str, sc1_bases: set = frozenset(), plain_stores: set = frozenset()
+):
+    """The kernel's code with tagged labels, s_endpgm → exit branch, sc1
+    stores (except through the plain_stores base SGPRs), sc1 on loads through
+    the given base SGPRs; and its VGPR / AGPR / LDS use."""
+    src, name = k["src"], k["name"]
+    body = src.split(f"\n{name}:\n", 1)[1].split("\n.Lfunc_end:", 1)[0]
+    out = []
+    for ln in body.split("\n"):
+        ln = re.sub(r"\.L(\w+)", lambda mt: f".L{tag}_{mt.group(1)}", ln)
+        if ln.strip() == "s_endpgm":
+            ln = f"  s_branch .L{tag}_exit"
+        elif re.match(r"\s*(buffer|global)_store", ln) and "sc1" not in ln:
+            b = re.search(r"s\[(\d+):\d+\]", ln)
+            if not (b and int(b.group(1)) in plain_stores):
+                ln += " sc1"
+        elif re.match(r"\s*(buffer|global)_load", ln) and "sc1" not in ln:
+            b = re.search(r"s\[(\d+):\d+\]", ln)
+            if b and int(b.group(1)) in sc1_bases:
+                ln += " sc1"
+        out.append(ln)
+    acc = int(re.search(r"\.amdhsa_accum_offset (\d+)", src).group(1))
+    tot = int(re.search(r"\.amdhsa_next_free_vgpr (\d+)", src).group(1))
+    lds = int(re.search(r"\.amdhsa_group_segment_fixed_size (\d+)", src).group(1))
+    sg = int(re.search(r"\.amdhsa_next_free_sgpr (\d+)", src).group(1))
+    assert acc <= 255 and sg <= 96, (tag, acc, sg)
+    return out, acc, tot - acc, lds
+
+
+def stamp(slot: int) -> list[str]:
+    """Wave 0, EXEC = lane 0: tl[CTA][slot] = s_memrealtime (low dword)."""
+    return [
+        f"  s_load_dwordx2 s[6:7], s[98:99], {OFF_TL:#x}",
+        "  s_memrealtime s[8:9]",
+        "  s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0)",
+        f"  s_mul_i32 s10, s97, {TL_SLOTS * 4}",
+        f"  s_add_u32 s10, s10, {slot * 4}",
+        "  v_mov_b32 v1, s10",
+        "  v_mov_b32 v2, s8",
+        "  global_store_dword v1, v2, s[6:7]",
+    ]
+
+
+def barrier(k: int, inv: str = "sc1") -> list[str]:

+    L = [

+        "  s_waitcnt vmcnt(0) lgkmcnt(0)",
+        "  s_barrier",
+        "  v_readfirstlane_b32 s4, v255",
+        "  s_lshr_b32 s4, s4, 6",
+        "  s_cmp_eq_u32 s4, 0",
+        f"  s_cbranch_scc0 {t}_follow",
+        "  s_mov_b64 exec, 1",
+    ]
+    L += stamp(2 * k - 1)
+    L += [
+        f"  s_load_dwordx2 s[4:5], s[98:99], {OFF_BAR:#x}",
+        "  s_add_u32 s96, s96, 1",
+        f"  s_and_b32 s8, s97, {GRP - 1}",
+        "  s_lshl_b32 s8, s8, 8",
+        "  s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0)",
+        "  s_add_u32 s9, s8, 256",
+        "  v_mov_b32 v1, s9",
+        "  v_mov_b32 v2, 1",
+        "  global_atomic_add v3, v1, v2, s[4:5] sc0 sc1",
+        "  s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)",
+        "  v_readfirstlane_b32 s10, v3",
+        "  s_add_u32 s10, s10, 1",
+        f"  s_mul_i32 s11, s96, {PER_GRP}",
+        "  s_cmp_eq_u32 s10, s11",
+        f"  s_cbranch_scc0 {t}_wait",
+        "  v_mov_b32 v1, 0",
+        "  global_atomic_add v3, v1, v2, s[4:5] sc0 sc1",
+        "  s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)",
+        "  v_readfirstlane_b32 s10, v3",
+        "  s_add_u32 s10, s10, 1",
+        f"  s_mul_i32 s11, s96, {GRP}",
+        "  s_cmp_eq_u32 s10, s11",
+        f"  s_cbranch_scc0 {t}_wait",
+        "  v_mov_b32 v4, s96",
+    ]

+        "  v_mov_b32 v1, s9",

+        "  s_cmp_ge_i32 s10, 0",
+        f"  s_cbranch_scc1 {t}_done",
+        "  s_sub_u32 s12, s12, 1",
+        "  s_cmp_eq_u32 s12, 0",

+
+def run_body(tag: str, body: list[str], grid, base: int, bit: int) -> list[str]:
+    def enter(cta: str):
+        return [
+            f"  s_add_u32 s0, s98, {base}",
+            "  s_addc_u32 s1, s99, 0",
+            f"  s_mov_b32 s2, {cta}",
+            "  v_mov_b32 v0, v255",
+            "  s_mov_b64 exec, -1",
+            "  s_nop 1",
+        ]  # readfirstlane of v0 needs a wait state
+
+    leave = [
+        f".L{tag}_exit:",
+        "  s_mov_b64 exec, -1",
+        "  s_waitcnt vmcnt(0) lgkmcnt(0)",
+    ]
+    L = [
+        f"  s_load_dwordx2 s[4:5], s[98:99], {OFF_M:#x}",
+        "  s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0)",  # s4 = m, s5 = knock
+        f"  s_bitcmp1_b32 s5, {bit}",
+        f"  s_cbranch_scc1 .L{tag}_skip",
+    ]
+    nv, first, cnt = grid if isinstance(grid, tuple) else (grid, 0, NCU)
+    if nv == "comb":
+        L += [
+            "  s_mul_i32 s101, s4, 640",
+            "  s_add_u32 s101, s101, 255",
+            "  s_lshr_b32 s101, s101, 8",
+        ]
+    elif nv == "m":
+        L += ["  s_mov_b32 s101, s4"]
+    else:
+        L += [f"  s_mov_b32 s101, {nv}"]
+    if first or cnt < NCU:
+        L += [
+            f"  s_sub_u32 s100, s97, {first}",
+            f"  s_cmp_ge_u32 s100, {cnt}",
+            f"  s_cbranch_scc1 .L{tag}_skip",
+        ]
+    else:
+        L += ["  s_mov_b32 s100, s97"]
+    L += [
+        f".L{tag}_virt:",
+        "  s_cmp_ge_u32 s100, s101",
+        f"  s_cbranch_scc1 .L{tag}_skip",
+    ]
+    L += (
+        enter("s100")
+        + body
+        + leave
+        + [f"  s_add_u32 s100, s100, {cnt}", f"  s_branch .L{tag}_virt"]
+    )
+    return L + [f".L{tag}_skip:"]
+
+
+def source(name: str = "ffn_k2", coh: str = "plain", layout: str = "base"):
+    """coh: "plain" | "loads" | "inv" | "sc0" (module docstring); layout: see phases()."""
+    coh = {"none": "plain"}.get(coh, coh)
+    inv = {"plain": "", "loads": "", "inv": "sc1", "sc0": "sc0"}[coh]
+    phs = phases(layout)
+    opts = set(layout.split("+"))

+        for tag, k, _ in ph:
+            args += [(f"{tag}.{n}", kind) for n, kind in k["ka"].args]

+    A("  s_mov_b32 s97, s2")
+    A("  v_mov_b32 v255, v0")

+        for off in range(0, ka.size, 64):
+            A(f"  s_load_dwordx16 s[4:19], s[0:1], {off:#x}")
+        A("  s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0)")

+    A("  s_lshr_b32 s4, s4, 6")
+    A("  s_cmp_eq_u32 s4, 0")
+    A("  s_cbranch_scc0 .Lstarted")
+    A("  s_mov_b64 exec, 1")
+    A(f"  s_load_dwordx2 s[4:5], s[98:99], {OFF_BAR:#x}")
+    A(f"  s_and_b32 s8, s97, {GRP - 1}")
+    A("  s_lshl_b32 s8, s8, 8")
+    A("  s_add_u32 s8, s8, 4352")
+    A("  v_mov_b32 v1, s8")
+    A("  s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0)")
+    A("  global_load_dword v3, v1, s[4:5] sc1")
+    A("  s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)")
+    A("  v_readfirstlane_b32 s96, v3")
+    c += stamp(0)
+    A("  s_mov_b64 exec, -1")

+    for i, ph in enumerate(phs):
+        for tag, k, grid in ph:

+            )

+            )

+            assert all(

+            bit += 1

+    A("  s_cbranch_scc0 .Lend")
+    A("  s_mov_b64 exec, 1")

+    A(".Lend:")
+    A("  s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)")
+    A("  s_endpgm")
+    src = kernel_source(
+        name, c, ka, lds=lds, vgprs=256, agprs=(ag + 3) // 4 * 4, sgprs=102, block=256
+    )
+    return dict(name=name, src=src, ka=ka, lds=lds, vgprs=vg, agprs=ag)

+"""Build, load and launch a generated gfx950 kernel. One ``KArgs`` spec gives
+the asm kernarg offsets, the code-object metadata and the host packing, so the
+two sides can't disagree."""
+
+import collections
+import ctypes
+import struct
+
+RSRC3 = 0x00020000  # buffer resource dword 3: gfx9 raw dword format
+
+
+class KArgs:
+    """Ordered kernargs: ("name", "ptr") 8 B or ("name", "u32") 4 B, natural
+    alignment, in declaration order."""
+
+    def __init__(self, *args: tuple[str, str]):
+        self.args, self.off, o = list(args), {}, 0
+        for name, kind in args:
+            size = 8 if kind == "ptr" else 4
+            o = (o + size - 1) // size * size
+            self.off[name] = o
+            o += size
+        self.size = (o + 7) // 8 * 8
+
+    def pack(self, **vals) -> bytes:
+        buf = bytearray(self.size)
+        for name, kind in self.args:
+            v = vals[name]
+            if kind == "ptr":
+                struct.pack_into(
+                    "<Q",
+                    buf,
+                    self.off[name],
+                    v.data_ptr() if hasattr(v, "data_ptr") else int(v),
+                )
+            else:
+                struct.pack_into("<I", buf, self.off[name], int(v) & 0xFFFFFFFF)
+        return bytes(buf)
+
+    def metadata(self) -> str:
+        out = []
+        for name, kind in self.args:
+            if kind == "ptr":
+                out.append(
+                    f"      - {{ .name: {name}, .size: 8, .offset: {self.off[name]}, "
+                    ".value_kind: global_buffer, .address_space: global }"
+                )
+            else:
+                out.append(
+                    f"      - {{ .name: {name}, .size: 4, .offset: {self.off[name]}, .value_kind: by_value }}"
+                )
+        return "\n".join(out)
+
+
+def kernel_source(
+    name: str,
+    body: list[str],
+    ka: KArgs,
+    *,
+    lds: int,
+    vgprs: int,
+    agprs: int,
+    sgprs: int,
+    block: int,
+) -> str:
+    acc_off = (vgprs + 3) // 4 * 4
+    total = acc_off + agprs
+    assert vgprs <= 256 and agprs <= 256 and total <= 512, (vgprs, agprs)
+    return f""".amdgcn_target "amdgcn-amd-amdhsa--gfx950"

+.globl {name}
+.p2align 8
+.type {name},@function
+{name}:
+{chr(10).join(body)}
+.Lfunc_end:
+.size {name}, .Lfunc_end-{name}
+
+.rodata
+.p2align 6
+.amdhsa_kernel {name}
+  .amdhsa_group_segment_fixed_size {lds}
+  .amdhsa_kernarg_size {ka.size}
+  .amdhsa_user_sgpr_kernarg_segment_ptr 1
+  .amdhsa_system_sgpr_workgroup_id_x 1
+  .amdhsa_system_vgpr_workitem_id 0
+  .amdhsa_next_free_vgpr {total}
+  .amdhsa_accum_offset {acc_off}
+  .amdhsa_next_free_sgpr {sgprs}

+.end_amdhsa_kernel

+.amdgpu_metadata
+---
+amdhsa.version: [ 1, 2 ]
+amdhsa.kernels:
+  - .name: {name}
+    .symbol: {name}.kd
+    .kernarg_segment_size: {ka.size}
+    .kernarg_segment_align: 8
+    .group_segment_fixed_size: {lds}
+    .private_segment_fixed_size: 0
+    .wavefront_size: 64
+    .sgpr_count: {sgprs}
+    .vgpr_count: {total}
+    .agpr_count: {agprs}

+.end_amdgpu_metadata

+
+
+class Kernel:
+    def __init__(self, name: str, src: str, ka: KArgs):
+        from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.asm.kernels.build import _check, build, hip
+
+        self.name, self.ka, self._check, self.h = name, ka, _check, hip()
+        img = build(src, name)
+        self._img = ctypes.create_string_buffer(img, len(img))
+        self.mod, self.fn = ctypes.c_void_p(), ctypes.c_void_p()
+        _check(
+            self.h.hipModuleLoadData(ctypes.byref(self.mod), self._img),
+            "hipModuleLoadData",
+        )
+        _check(
+            self.h.hipModuleGetFunction(ctypes.byref(self.fn), self.mod, name.encode()),
+            "hipModuleGetFunction",
+        )
+        # recent launches' kernarg memory (bounded: a server launches forever)
+        self._keep: collections.deque = collections.deque(maxlen=4096)
+
+    def __call__(self, grid: int, block: int, **vals) -> None:
+        """KernelParams launch: an array of pointers to each argument value; HIP copies them using the code
+        object's argument metadata (at launch, or at capture for a graph node)."""
+        import torch
+
+        cells = []
+        for name, kind in self.ka.args:
+            v = vals[name]
+            if kind == "ptr":
+                cells.append(
+                    ctypes.c_uint64(v.data_ptr() if hasattr(v, "data_ptr") else int(v))

+            else:
+                cells.append(ctypes.c_uint32(int(v) & 0xFFFFFFFF))

+            *[ctypes.cast(ctypes.pointer(x), ctypes.c_void_p) for x in cells]
+        )

+        self._check(
+            self.h.hipModuleLaunchKernel(
+                self.fn,
+                grid,
+                1,
+                1,
+                block,
+                1,
+                1,
+                0,
+                torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream,
+                params,
+                None,
+            ),
+            "hipModuleLaunchKernel",
+        )
+
+
+def rsrc(
+    sbase: int, ptr_sgpr: int, nbytes_sgpr: int | None = None, nbytes: int | None = None
+) -> list[str]:
+    """Buffer resource in s[sbase:sbase+3] from a 64-bit pointer in
+    s[ptr_sgpr:ptr_sgpr+1] and a byte size (SGPR or constant)."""
+    n = f"s{nbytes_sgpr}" if nbytes_sgpr is not None else str(nbytes)
+    return [
+        f"  s_mov_b32 s{sbase}, s{ptr_sgpr}",
+        f"  s_and_b32 s{sbase + 1}, s{ptr_sgpr + 1}, 0xffff",
+        f"  s_mov_b32 s{sbase + 2}, {n}",
+        f"  s_mov_b32 s{sbase + 3}, {RSRC3:#x}",
+    ]

+"""Routed-MoE combine: out[token][r] = bf16(Σ_k y[token*6 + k][r]) over the
+token's 6 picks (y already weighted, from moe_down1.py). A pick with id < 0
+is skipped by pointing its loads out of range (they read 0).
+
+One thread per (token, 8 rows): 6 id loads, 12 dwordx4 y loads, one 16 B store.
+add=True (part, the MoE's output before its all-reduce): out =
+bf16(bf16(Σ y) + add), add bf16 [M, 5120] (the shared expert), as vLLM's bf16
+``routed + shared``.
+"""
+
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.asm.kernels.kmod import KArgs, kernel_source, rsrc
+
+H = 5120
+KA = KArgs(
+    ("y", "ptr"),
+    ("ids", "ptr"),
+    ("out", "ptr"),
+    ("m", "u32"),
+    ("y_bytes", "u32"),
+    ("ids_bytes", "u32"),
+    ("out_bytes", "u32"),
+)
+KA_ADD = KArgs(*KA.args, ("add", "ptr"), ("add_bytes", "u32"))
+
+
+def source(name: str | None = None, add: bool = False, y_bf16: bool = False):
+    """y_bf16: y bf16 [P, 5120] (moe_down1 y_bf16), one dwordx4
+    per pick, widened to f32 and summed in the same order."""
+    name = name or ("moe_combine_add" if add else "moe_combine") + (
+        "_yb" if y_bf16 else ""
+    )
+    yb = 2 if y_bf16 else 4
+    ka = KA_ADD if add else KA
+    c = []
+    A = c.append
+    A("  s_load_dwordx8 s[4:11], s[0:1], 0x0")  # y, ids, out, m, y_bytes
+    A("  s_load_dwordx2 s[12:13], s[0:1], 0x20")  # ids_bytes, out_bytes
+    if add:
+        A(f"  s_load_dwordx2 s[36:37], s[0:1], {ka.off['add']:#x}")
+        A(f"  s_load_dword s38, s[0:1], {ka.off['add_bytes']:#x}")
+    A("  s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0)")
+    c += rsrc(16, 4, nbytes_sgpr=11)
+    c += rsrc(20, 6, nbytes_sgpr=12)
+    c += rsrc(24, 8, nbytes_sgpr=13)
+    if add:
+        c += rsrc(40, 36, nbytes_sgpr=38)
+    A("  s_lshl_b32 s28, s2, 8")
+    A("  v_add_u32 v1, s28, v0")  # gid
+    A(f"  s_mul_i32 s29, s10, {H // 8}")  # total threads
+    A("  v_cmp_gt_u32 vcc, s29, v1")
+    A("  s_and_saveexec_b64 s[30:31], vcc")
+    A("  s_cbranch_execz .Lend")
+    A("  s_mov_b32 s32, 0xcccccccd")
+    A("  v_lshrrev_b32 v2, 7, v1")
+    A("  v_mul_hi_u32 v2, v2, s32")
+    A("  v_lshrrev_b32 v2, 2, v2")  # token = gid / 640
+    A(f"  v_mul_u32_u24 v3, {H // 8}, v2")
+    A("  v_sub_u32 v3, v1, v3")  # chunk
+    A("  v_mul_u32_u24 v4, 24, v2")  # ids offset token*6*4
+    for k in range(6):
+        A(f"  buffer_load_dword v{10 + k}, v4, s[20:23], 0 offen offset:{4 * k}")
+    A("  v_mov_b32 v5, 0x7fff0000")
+    A(f"  v_mul_u32_u24 v6, {6 * H * yb}, v2")  # y row of pick token*6
+    A(f"  v_lshl_add_u32 v6, v3, {4 if y_bf16 else 5}, v6")  # + chunk * 32 B (16 B)
+    A("  s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)")
+    for k in range(6):
+        A(f"  v_add_u32 v7, {k * H * yb}, v6")
+        A(f"  v_cmp_le_i32 vcc, 0, v{10 + k}")
+        A(f"  v_cndmask_b32 v{16 + k}, v5, v7, vcc")
+    A(f"  v_mul_u32_u24 v8, {H * 2}, v2")
+    A("  v_lshl_add_u32 v8, v3, 4, v8")  # out / add offset
+    if add:
+        A("  buffer_load_dwordx4 v[76:79], v8, s[40:43], 0 offen")
+    for k in range(6):
+        b = 24 + 8 * k
+        if y_bf16:
+            A(f"  buffer_load_dwordx4 v[{b + 4}:{b + 7}], v{16 + k}, s[16:19], 0 offen")
+        else:
+            A(f"  buffer_load_dwordx4 v[{b}:{b + 3}], v{16 + k}, s[16:19], 0 offen")
+            A(
+                f"  buffer_load_dwordx4 v[{b + 4}:{b + 7}], v{16 + k}, s[16:19], 0 offen offset:16"
+            )
+    A("  s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)")
+    if y_bf16:  # bf16 pairs → f32: element 2q = d << 16, 2q + 1 = d & 0xffff0000
+        for k in range(6):
+            b = 24 + 8 * k
+            for q in range(4):
+                A(f"  v_lshlrev_b32 v{b + 2 * q}, 16, v{b + 4 + q}")
+                A(f"  v_and_b32 v{b + 2 * q + 1}, 0xffff0000, v{b + 4 + q}")
+    for k in range(1, 6):
+        for i in range(8):
+            A(f"  v_add_f32 v{24 + i}, v{24 + i}, v{24 + 8 * k + i}")
+    for q in range(4):
+        A(f"  v_cvt_pk_bf16_f32 v{72 + q}, v{24 + 2 * q}, v{25 + 2 * q}")

+        for q in range(4):
+            A(f"  v_lshlrev_b32 v80, 16, v{72 + q}")
+            A(f"  v_and_b32 v81, 0xffff0000, v{72 + q}")
+            A(f"  v_lshlrev_b32 v82, 16, v{76 + q}")
+            A(f"  v_and_b32 v83, 0xffff0000, v{76 + q}")
+            A("  v_add_f32 v80, v80, v82")
+            A("  v_add_f32 v81, v81, v83")

+    A(".Lend:")
+    A("  s_endpgm")
+    src = kernel_source(
+        name,
+        c,
+        ka,
+        lds=0,
+        vgprs=88 if add else 80,
+        agprs=0,
+        sgprs=48 if add else 40,
+        block=256,
+    )
+    return dict(name=name, src=src, ka=ka)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+# mypy: ignore-errors
+# ruff: noqa: E501  (one asm instruction or template line per source line)
+"""Routed-MoE stage 2 (down), v1: expert-major, per-pick outputs.
+
+v0 (moe_down.py) took units (16-row block, pick group) row-block-major: each
+unit was a 4.5 KB w2 chunk of a different expert (scattered reads) and the
+ring held ~2 units per wave: 4.1-4.6 TB/s, and removing the h gathers gained
+only 2-9%. v1 streams each expert's w2 contiguously instead:
+
+- Units (pick group g, chunk c of 16 row blocks = 256 output rows), group-
+  major, contiguous equal ranges per CTA; wave w takes row blocks 4w..4w+3 of
+  the chunk (18 KB of w2, contiguous apart from the K-padding half-tiles).
+- Step = one row block: 5 K-tiles (the last half padding: lanes 0..31 loaded,
+  the rest zeroed) into an 8-step AGPR ring; A scales (one dword per row-block
+  pair and 2 K-tiles) on even steps; the odd block's scales are byte 1/3 of
+  the same dword, so op_sel is static.
+- The group's h (B fragments, 5 tiles × 8 VGPRs + 2 scale dwords + the pick's
+  weight) stays in VGPRs; the next group's is prefetched only when the group
+  changes (two unit-body variants: exact s_waitcnt counts).
+- Output: y[p][row] = w_p · (W2 h_p)[row], fp32, one dwordx4 store per lane
+  per step (lane t + 16 gq: rows 4 gq..4 gq+3 of pick t). Two accumulator sets
+  alternate, so a step's result is read while the next step's MFMAs run.
+  moe_combine.py sums each token's 6 rows into bf16.
+
+Tables / tensors:
+- units int32 [n, 20]: e, c, gid, 0, picks[16] (p = token*6 + k, or -1)
+- h fp8 [P, 576]; hs uint8 [P, 4, 8]; wts fp32 [P]; y fp32 [P, 5120]
+"""
+
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.asm.kernels import gtable
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.asm.kernels.kmod import KArgs, kernel_source, rsrc
+
+H, E = 5120, 384
+W2_E = H * 320
+S2_E = H * 24
+CH = 16  # row blocks per chunk
+NCH = 320 // CH  # 20 chunks
+
+KA = KArgs(
+    ("w2", "ptr"),
+    ("s2", "ptr"),
+    ("h", "ptr"),
+    ("hs", "ptr"),
+    ("wts", "ptr"),
+    ("groups", "ptr"),
+    ("y", "ptr"),
+    ("counts", "ptr"),
+    ("h_bytes", "u32"),
+    ("hs_bytes", "u32"),
+    ("wts_bytes", "u32"),
+    ("y_bytes", "u32"),
+)
+
+
+KA_COMB = KArgs(
+    *KA.args,
+    ("ids", "ptr"),
+    ("shared", "ptr"),
+    ("part", "ptr"),
+    ("sync", "ptr"),
+    ("m", "u32"),
+)
+PSTRIDE = 4  # sync: one progress word per CTA, packed (8 lines per aggregator poll)
+NAGG = 8  # aggregator combiners (CTAs 0..7): global min, own line each
+AGG_OFF = PSTRIDE * gtable.GRID
+CTR_OFF = AGG_OFF + 128 * NAGG  # then per-CTA seq counters
+TL_OFF = CTR_OFF + 4 * gtable.GRID  # timeline (s_memrealtime low dwords), 16 per CTA:
+TL_WORDS = 16  # 0 start (wave 0), 1-4 stage-2 wave ends, 5-9 chunk go, 10 combiner end
+SYNC_BYTES = TL_OFF + 4 * TL_WORDS * gtable.GRID
+
+
+def source(
+    split: str = "ceil",
+    D: int = 4,
+    grid: int = gtable.GRID,
+    PER_MAX: int = 128,
+    w_pol: str = "nt",
+    name: str | None = None,
+    early_w: int = 0,
+    knock: str = "",
+    y_pol: str = "",
+    counts_vec: bool = False,
+    comb: bool = False,
+    csleep: int = 1,
+    cknock: str = "",
+    cg: int = 4,
+    asleep: int = 1,
+    y_bf16: bool = False,
+    y_batch: bool = False,
+    y_exec: bool = False,
+    s_pol: str = "",
+):
+    """Comb (K2 v2b, split "rr" only): a 5th wave per CTA combines column chunks
+    while stage 2 runs (see combiner()); kernargs KA_COMB.
+    early_w: issue the first D-1 steps' weight loads before the h gather.
+    knock (perf experiments only, wrong results): "s" no y stores, "m" no MFMAs,
+    "a" no A-scale loads, "c" stores to one contiguous L2-resident 1 KB per wave,
+    "E" no stores during the stream, then each wave writes y_bytes / 1024 contiguous
+    bytes (512 B dwordx2 stores) after its last step,
+    "h" 8 B (bf16-sized) stores at the real addresses, "C" bf16-sized stores
+    (dwordx2, every lane) to one L2-resident 512 B per wave.
+    y_bf16: y in bf16, [P, 5120] (half the bytes written and read
+    back by the combine; the fp32 stores cost ~3 bytes of weight stream each):
+    one dwordx2 per lane per step, the same instruction counts.
+    y_batch (with y_bf16): a unit's 4 results go out together at the next
+    unit's first step (steps 0-2 parked in 6 VGPRs). vmcnt retires in issue
+    order and a store under load takes ~5-10k clk to complete (measured),
+    so every weight load issued after a store waits for it: once per unit
+    instead of once per step.
+    y_exec (with y_bf16): the y store runs under EXEC = the lanes with a pick
+    (vY != the out-of-range v0) instead of sending every lane to the TA.
+    s_pol: cache policy of the A-scale loads (no reuse; plain by default)."""
+    SPU = 4  # steps (row blocks) per unit per wave
+    UST = grid if split == "rr" else 1  # unit stride of a CTA
+    # D ≤ SPU keeps a prefetch's effect on the wait counts inside its own unit;
+    # D | SPU keeps ring slots static (slot = step % D).
+    assert D <= SPU and SPU % D == 0
+    UPI = 1
+    LPS = 5 + (
+        0 if "a" in knock else 3
+    )  # loads per step: W 5 + A scales 3 (every step: no slot race)
+    XL = 10 + 2 + 1  # h prefetch: 10 B + 2 SB + 1 weight
+    R = 80
+    TBL = (PER_MAX * R + 255) // 256 * 256
+    lds = (
+        TBL if split != "rr" else (E + 6 * 256 // 16) * R
+    )  # rr: the whole table (NG <= E + P / 16)
+    PLDS = lds  # comb: 4 progress slots (one per stage-2 wave)
+    if comb:
+        lds += 16
+    assert not comb or (split == "rr" and grid == gtable.GRID and D == 4), (
+        "comb: rr split, grid 256, D 4"
+    )
+    name = (
+        name
+        or f"moe_down1{'c' + str(csleep) + 'a' + str(asleep) + cknock + '_g' + str(cg) if comb else ''}_{split}_d{D}_g{grid}{'_' + w_pol.replace(' ', '') if w_pol else ''}_e{early_w}{'_k' + knock if knock else ''}{'_y' + y_pol.replace(' ', '') if y_pol else ''}{'_yb' if y_bf16 else ''}{'_bt' if y_batch else ''}{'_ye' if y_exec else ''}{'_s' + s_pol.replace(' ', '') if s_pol else ''}"
+    )
+    pol = f" {w_pol}" if w_pol else ""
+
+    # VGPRs: v0 OOB, v1 lane, v2 lane*16, v3 lane*16+4096, v4 lane*4, v5 t, v6 gq
+    vB, vS, vT, vY, vP = (
+        8,
+        9,
+        10,
+        11,
+        12,
+    )  # current group: h off, hs off, wts off, y off, p
+    nB, nS, nT, nY, nP = 13, 14, 15, 16, 17
+    SA0 = 18  # SA ring: 3 per slot
+    XC = SA0 + 3 * D + 1
+    XC += XC % 2
+    XN = XC + 44
+    TMP = XN + 44
+    t = [TMP + i for i in range(16)]
+    vgprs = TMP + 16
+    assert not y_batch or (
+        y_bf16 and split != "rr" and not comb and D == SPU == 4 and not knock
+    ), "y_batch"
+    hold = (
+        [vgprs + i for i in range(6)] if y_batch else []
+    )  # bf16 y of a unit's steps 0-2
+    vgprs += len(hold)
+    assert vgprs <= 256, vgprs
+    HB, HSB, HW = 0, 40, 42  # offsets inside an h buffer: B, SB (2), weight
+    WR0 = 8  # AGPRs: acc a[0:3], a[4:7]; ring a[8 + 20 * slot]
+    agprs = WR0 + 20 * D
+
+    def sa(s):
+        return SA0 + 3 * (s % D)
+
+    c = []
+    A = c.append
+    A("  s_load_dwordx16 s[4:19], s[0:1], 0x0")
+    A("  s_load_dwordx4 s[20:23], s[0:1], 0x40")
+    A("  v_readfirstlane_b32 s48, v0")
+    A("  s_lshr_b32 s48, s48, 6")
+    if comb:
+        # wave 4 combines; the stage-2 waves publish progress words (sync + 4 (4 b + w)), seq from ctr[b]
+        A("  s_cmp_eq_u32 s48, 4")
+        A("  s_cbranch_scc1 .Lcomb")
+        A(f"  s_load_dwordx2 s[88:89], s[0:1], {KA_COMB.off['sync']:#x}")
+        A("  s_lshl_b32 s95, s2, 2")
+        A(f"  s_add_u32 s95, s95, {CTR_OFF}")
+        A("  s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0)")
+        A("  s_load_dword s94, s[88:89], s95")
+        A("  s_lshl_b32 s95, s48, 2")
+        A(f"  v_mov_b32 v{t[14]}, {PLDS}")
+        A(f"  v_add_u32 v{t[14]}, s95, v{t[14]}")  # my LDS progress slot
+        A("  s_memrealtime s[68:69]")
+        A("  s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0)")
+        A("  s_add_u32 s94, s94, 1")
+        A("  s_lshl_b32 s94, s94, 20")  # this launch's seq << 20
+        A("  s_add_u32 s95, s94, s2")  # nothing done yet: next unit = my first (b)
+        A(f"  v_mov_b32 v{t[15]}, s95")
+        A(
+            f"  ds_write_b32 v{t[14]}, v{t[15]}"
+        )  # before range_and_copy's lgkmcnt(0) + s_barrier
+    A("  v_and_b32 v1, 63, v0")
+    A("  v_lshlrev_b32 v2, 4, v1")
+    A("  v_add_u32 v3, 0x1000, v2")
+    A("  v_lshlrev_b32 v4, 2, v1")
+    A("  v_and_b32 v5, 15, v1")
+    A("  v_lshrrev_b32 v6, 4, v1")
+    A("  s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0)")
+    # kernargs: w2 s[4:5] s2 s[6:7] h s[8:9] hs s[10:11] wts s[12:13] units s[14:15] y s[16:17]
+    #           nunits s18 per s19 h_bytes s20 hs_bytes s21 wts_bytes s22 y_bytes s23
+    c += rsrc(24, 4, nbytes=-1)
+    c += rsrc(28, 6, nbytes=-1)
+    c += rsrc(32, 8, nbytes_sgpr=20)
+    c += rsrc(36, 10, nbytes_sgpr=21)
+    c += rsrc(40, 12, nbytes_sgpr=22)
+    c += rsrc(44, 16, nbytes_sgpr=23)
+    c += gtable.range_and_copy(
+        20,
+        counts=18,
+        groups=14,
+        tv=[t[0], t[1], t[2]],

+    granules. The 256 combiner waves form CG groups: wave b is in group q = b % CG, which owns chunks q, q + CG,
+    ...; inside a chunk the group's 256/CG waves split the granules evenly (per = ceil(M*32 CG / 256) <= 128,
+    two 64-lane passes, loaded together).

+    c += rsrc(28, 6, nbytes=-1)

+    c += rsrc(36, 10, nbytes_sgpr=21)

+        o = gtable.decode(18, u_sgpr, Gs, J)
+        o += [

+            f"  ds_read_b32 v{t2}, v{t0}",
+            f"  v_lshlrev_b32 v{t0}, 2, v4",
+            f"  v_add_u32 v{t0}, s76, v{t0}",

+            f"  v_readfirstlane_b32 s77, v{t2}",
+            f"  s_mul_i32 s78, s77, {W13_E}",
+            f"  s_mul_i32 s79, s{J}, {4 * KT * 1024}",
+            "  s_add_u32 s78, s78, s79",

+        o = []

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+# mypy: ignore-errors
+# ruff: noqa: E501  (one asm instruction or template line per source line)
+"""Several kernels as one launch, side by side: CTAs first ..
+first + n - 1 run body ``tag`` with s2 = CTA - first, s[0:1] at that body's
+block of the combined kernargs (laid out exactly as the body's own KArgs,
+names prefixed ``tag.``), v0 = thread id. Bodies are the kernels' code
+unchanged except for their labels (``.Ltag_*``); ``s_endpgm`` stays (a CTA
+runs one body). The launch gets the bodies' largest VGPR / AGPR / SGPR / LDS
+counts and block size, so co-residency is the largest body's.
+
+    k = multi.source("ffn_prep_sdn", [("prep", prep_k, 1), ("sdn", sdn_k, 160)])
+    Kernel(k["name"], k["src"], k["ka"])(k["grid"], k["block"], **{"prep.x": .., "sdn.w": ..})
+"""
+
+import regex as re
+
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.asm.kernels.kmod import KArgs, kernel_source
+
+
+def _use(src: str, key: str) -> int:
+    return int(re.search(rf"\.amdhsa_{key} (\d+)", src).group(1))
+
+
+def source(name: str, parts: list[tuple[str, dict, int]]):
+    """One launch of ``parts``: (tag, a kernel generator's dict with name / src
+    / ka, CTA count) each."""
+    args, bases, c = [], {}, []
+    for tag, k, _ in parts:
+        args += [(f"{tag}.{n}", kind) for n, kind in k["ka"].args]
+    ka = KArgs(*args)
+    vg = ag = sg = lds = 0
+    block = 0
+    first = 0
+    for i, (tag, k, n) in enumerate(parts):
+        base = ka.off[f"{tag}.{k['ka'].args[0][0]}"]
+        assert all(
+            ka.off[f"{tag}.{a}"] - base == k["ka"].off[a] for a, _ in k["ka"].args
+        ), tag
+        bases[tag] = (first, n, base)
+        first += n
+    grid = first
+    # dispatch: the last part takes the rest
+    for tag, k, n in parts[:-1]:
+        f, _, _ = bases[tag]
+        c.append(f"  s_cmp_lt_u32 s2, {f + n}")
+        c.append(f"  s_cbranch_scc1 .L{tag}_enter")
+    c.append(f"  s_branch .L{parts[-1][0]}_enter")
+    for tag, k, n in parts:
+        src, kname = k["src"], k["name"]
+        f, _, base = bases[tag]
+        body = src.split(f"\n{kname}:\n", 1)[1].split("\n.Lfunc_end:", 1)[0]
+        c.append(f".L{tag}_enter:")
+        if f:
+            c.append(f"  s_sub_u32 s2, s2, {f}")
+        if base:
+            c += [f"  s_add_u32 s0, s0, {base}", "  s_addc_u32 s1, s1, 0"]
+        c += [
+            re.sub(r"\.L(\w+)", lambda mt, tag=tag: f".L{tag}_{mt.group(1)}", ln)
+            for ln in body.split("\n")
+        ]
+        acc = _use(src, "accum_offset")
+        vg, ag = max(vg, acc), max(ag, _use(src, "next_free_vgpr") - acc)
+        sg, lds = (
+            max(sg, _use(src, "next_free_sgpr")),
+            max(lds, _use(src, "group_segment_fixed_size")),
+        )
+        block = max(block, k.get("block", 256))
+    src = kernel_source(
+        name,
+        c,
+        ka,
+        lds=lds,
+        vgprs=vg,
+        agprs=(ag + 3) // 4 * 4,
+        sgprs=min(max(sg, 16), 102),
+        block=block,
+    )
+    return dict(name=name, src=src, ka=ka, grid=grid, block=block, vgprs=vg, agprs=ag)

+"""q/kv RMSNorm, q MXFP8 and the SWA KV insert (front part):
+the step between wqkv (gemv8 WQKV, bf16 qr_kv [M, 1792]) and wq_b.
+
+One wave per token (4 per CTA). Lane l loads 32 bf16 of the token's row:
+lanes 0..39 the q block l (dims 32l ..), lanes 40..55 the kv dims 32 (l − 40) ..
+- RMSNorm as vLLM's Triton kernel: fp32, y = bf16((x · rsqrt(Σx²/n + eps)) · w)
+  (``v_rsq_f32``; Σx² over the group's lanes by DPP / permlane, fixed order).
+- q: MXFP8 per 32 dims (ceil rule) → qr in gemv8's frag layout (wq_b's x).
+- kv: GPT-J RoPE on dims 448.. in fp32, bf16; then vLLM's fp8_ds_mla record
+  (fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cu): per 64 dims exponent =
+  ceil(log2(max(absmax, 1e-4) / 448)) with an IEEE-rounded quotient and
+  ``v_log_f32``, codes = e4m3(clamp(x · 2^-exponent, ±448)); RoPE dims stay
+  bf16; scale bytes exponent + 127, byte 7 = 0. Written to the SWA cache at
+  slot_mapping[t] (block = slot >> bsl, row = slot & (bs − 1)) unless < 0.
+"""
+
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.asm.kernels.kmod import KArgs, kernel_source
+
+QL, KVD, NOPE = 1280, 512, 448
+KGQ = QL // 128  # wq_b's x: K tiles
+
+KA = KArgs(
+    ("qr_kv", "ptr"),
+    ("qw", "ptr"),
+    ("kvw", "ptr"),
+    ("pos", "ptr"),
+    ("cs", "ptr"),
+    ("slots", "ptr"),
+    ("cache", "ptr"),
+    ("xq", "ptr"),
+    ("xs", "ptr"),
+    ("m", "u32"),
+    ("eps", "u32"),
+    ("stride", "u32"),
+    ("bsl", "u32"),
+)

inline_comments.body:
PR size: `decode.py` only ever builds `K1Runner(v3=True)` and calls `weights(..., v3=True)` / `attend(..., v3=True)`, so the non-v3 path can't be reached:

- `front()`, `idx_q()` and `back()` have no callers (only `front_v3`, `idx_q3` and `back_ar` are used).
- `self.k_attn` / `self.k_attn_fx` are only used in `attend`'s non-v3 branch.
- `k_g` is built for every entry of `GEMVS`, including `wqkv` (v3 uses `WQKV32N` via `k_wqkv_mx`), `wq_b` and `idx_wq_b`. Those are only launched from the dead `front` / `idx_q`.

These kernels are still generated and assembled at startup on every rank, which adds build time and code objects for nothing. Could we drop the `v3` flag (always on), the non-v3 methods and branches, and the unused kernels? The same applies to any generator options in `attn_dec1.py` / `gemv8.py` that only these paths use.

Estimated gain (static reading, not measured):

- About 70 lines that are clearly dead in `k1_runner.py`: `front` (~25), `idx_q` (~6), `back` (~7), the `k_attn` / `k_attn_fx` construction and the non-v3 `attend` selection (~8), plus the `v3` flag plumbing in `__init__` / `_scratch` / `weights` (~20).
- About 10 lines for the `WQKV16` / `WQKV16N` configs and the `K1` mapping in `gemv8.py`.
- Likely another ~100-200 lines of generator branches only these kernels select (`attn_dec1.source` without `rr_scale` / `part_bf16`, the WQKV16 epilogues).

Roughly 80-280 lines in total. It also removes 2 attention kernels and 3 GEMV kernels from the startup build.

+"""K1, the attention half of a decoder layer (from the attention seam's
+inputs to the all-reduced attention output), in the pieces vLLM's breakable
+CUDA graph needs:
+
+    run = K1Runner(v3=True)
+    w = run.weights(layer, v3=True)
+    # captured: the seam (mHC pre-mix + norm) → (r_new, post, comb, y, pre)
+    outs = run.seam_v3(w, residual, sub, post_mix, res_mix, pre_mix)
+    # captured: wqkv, norms + SWA insert, wq_b
+    q = run.front_v3(w, m, positions, slots, swa_cache, swa_bs)
+    # eager break: sparse attention → o (frag)
+    run.attend(w, q, ..., v3=True)
+    # ... or vLLM's MXFP8 attention output → o (mixed steps)
+    run.from_attn_out(attn_out, m)
+    # captured: wo_a, wo_b with all-reduce #1 folded in
+    out = run.back_ar(w, m, pos, wob, wire)
+
+The v1 pieces (``seam``, ``front``, ``idx_q``, ``back``) serve the Engram
+seam and the v3 pieces' internals.
+
+After an index source's top-k, ``run.translate(...)`` maps it through the
+block table into the scratch's fixed-stride lists (token t at t·512, counts in
+``tk_lens``), which ``attend(.., fixed=True)`` reads instead of vLLM's ragged
+pack (4 launches). ``run.idx_logits(...)`` (kernels/idx_logits.py) computes
+the indexer's MXFP4 logits and writes the same lists from its top-512 in one
+launch, in place of vLLM's logits, top-k and translate (``idx_wide`` /
+``idx_gather``: wide rows and the candidate source / consumers).
+
+v3 (``K1Runner(v3=True)``):
+``seam_v3`` runs the seam main only (y' = MXFP8(x1 · attn_norm.w) into wqkv's
+x, no fin; post / comb / pre come back empty and are filled by ``front_v3``),
+``front_v3`` runs wqkv32n with the mixes waves (fin's mixes, rstd[t]) and wq_b
+with the kv wave (rstd applied, record + SWA insert); q stays without the q
+norm's rrms, which ``attend(.., v3=True)`` folds into its score scale (and
+``q_rr`` applies for vLLM's attention on mixed steps). The y it returns is a
+placeholder: on consumer layers vLLM only passes it on to our attention.
+Index layers on v3 (``seam_v3(.., idx=True)``): y is y' = bf16(x1 ·
+attn_norm.w) without rstd; the indexer's weights_proj reads it and its wq_b
+reads front_v3's q x (no rrms), both off by a positive per-token factor that
+the top-k selection doesn't see; comp_tail(rs_part=) scales the compressor
+GEMM's rows by rstd itself. ``idx_q`` runs after ``front_v3`` as after ``front``.
+
+Activations between the pieces stay in the runner's scratch in gemv8's frag
+layout (sized for M = 256, allocated once; layers run one after another on a
+stream, so they share it). Weights are frag-shuffled copies (gemv8.frag_w),
+~40 MB per layer.
+"""

+import struct

+import torch
+
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.asm.kernels import (

+    ffn_seam,
+    gemv8,
+    idx_logits,
+    idx_topk,
+    qkv_norm,
+)
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.asm.kernels.kmod import Kernel
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton

+H, MAX_M, HEADS, D = 5120, 256, 16, 512
+BF = torch.bfloat16
+ATTRS = {"wqkv": "fused_wqa_wkv", "wq_b": "wq_b", "wo_a": "wo_a", "wo_b": "wo_b"}
+GEMVS = {n: (gemv8.K1[n], a) for n, a in ATTRS.items()}
+GEMVS["idx_wq_b"] = (gemv8.IDX_WQ_B, "indexer.wq_b")
+
+
+def f32bits(v: float) -> int:
+    return struct.unpack("<I", struct.pack("<f", v))[0]

+gemv_mode = gemv8.k1_mode

+@triton.jit

+    out, lens, topk, topk_stride, req_of, valid, bt, bt_stride, bs, TOPK: tl.constexpr

+    t = tl.program_id(0)

PR size: `K2Runner` builds the generic `k2.phases(layout)` kernels first, then `_v3()` swaps most of them out: `seam` twice (v1 from `phases`, `source_v2()`, then `ffn_seam2_ug`), `fin` deleted, and `p3`, `ug`, `dn`, `comb`, `prep` and `rt` replaced or merged. So the replaced kernels are assembled for nothing. `mode` is asserted to be `"chain"`, and `layout` / `v3` are always the defaults.

That looks like leftover exploration code. Candidates to remove:

- `ffn_seam.source()` (v1, which the comment says `source_v2` matches bitwise).
- `k2.source()` and most of `k2.phases`' `layout` option matrix (`inv_ug`, `inv_dn`, `kpre`, `cost` / `ceil`, ...).
- The non-`counts_vec` / non-`y_bf16` / `ceil` variants in `moe_ug1.py` / `moe_down1.py` / `moe_combine.py`, if nothing else uses them.
- The `mode` / `layout` / `v3` constructor parameters.

Building the final kernel set directly would make the runner much easier to review, and it should cut a sizeable share of the ~16k lines.

Estimated gain (static reading, not measured):

- `ffn_seam.source` v1: ~200 lines, used only by `k2.phases`, which `_v3()` then replaces.
- `kernels/k2.py`: ~290 lines with no caller outside the file (the single-kernel cooperative machinery: `source`, `run_body`, `barrier`, `stamp`, `body_of`, `SKEL`, `BAR_BYTES`, `PLAIN_STORES`, `LAYOUTS`, `BODIES` / `NB`). The ~57-line `phases()` can be reduced to the two bodies still used (`prep`, `sdn`). In practice the whole 414-line file can go.
- `k2_runner.py`: ~40 lines of replace-and-assert scaffolding in `_v3()`, plus the `mode` / `layout` / `v3` plumbing.
- `ffn_route.source_p3`: the `v3=False` branches (~10-20 lines).
- The unused option matrix in `moe_ug1.py` / `moe_down1.py` / `moe_combine.py` (non-`counts_vec`, non-`rstd`, `ceil`, f32-y and the various `*_pol` / `knock` knobs): probably another ~100-300 lines, to be confirmed.

Roughly 650-900 lines in total. It also removes about 7 kernels that are built at startup and never launched.

PR size: `install()` turns on four independent features at once:

1. K2 (FFN half + all-reduce #2).
2. K1 (attention half + all-reduce #1).
3. The indexer logits + top-512 replacement (`_idx_topk_install`, which also brings `comp_tail.py`, `idx_logits.py` and `idx_topk.py`, about 3k lines with three width regimes).
4. The Engram side chain (`engram.py`, `eg_runner.py`, `eg_ag.py`).

Each one already falls back to vLLM on its own, so they could land as stacked PRs: e.g. K2 first, then K1, then the indexer top-k, then Engram. Each would carry its own TPOT delta and accuracy check. That would make 16k lines of generated assembly reviewable, and show which pieces carry the 1.15-1.54× gains. If some piece (e.g. the wide / gather top-k regimes for >72k context) contributes little, it could be dropped entirely.

Approximate size of each piece (`wc -l` on the PR head; `ffn_seam.py`, 1.2k lines, is shared by K1 and K2):

- Common plumbing: ~2.2k (`decode.py`, `ar_runner.py`, `ar2.py`, `kmod.py`, `build.py`).
- K2: ~4.1k (`k2_runner.py`, `k2.py`, `ffn_route.py`, `moe_*.py`, `multi.py`, `gtable.py`, `comb_ar.py`).
- K1: ~4.6k (`k1_runner.py`, `attn_dec1.py`, `gemv8.py`, `qkv_norm.py`, `wob_ar.py`).
- Indexer top-k + compressor tail: ~3.3k (`idx_logits.py`, `idx_topk.py`, `comp_tail.py`, plus ~170 lines in `decode.py`).
- Engram: ~0.85k (`engram.py`, `eg_runner.py`, `eg_ag.py`).

A K2-only first PR would be about 7.5k lines (common + K2 + `ffn_seam.py`), before the dead-code removals in the other comments. That is roughly half of the current diff.

Once `enabled()` returns True, the mono limit drops from 48 to 16 for the whole process. But the asm path can still decline a layer later, at `install()` time:

- K2 declines the DSpark draft layers (128 experts / top-3, `decode.py` `_k2_install`). Mono does serve them: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/20d7dd9ac15292357ed474856cf268af9dd730ba/vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/mono_decode.py#L397-L402
- K1 declines layers when the KV cache isn't `fp8_ds_mla` (e.g. `kv_mxfp8`), on dense / ratio-0 layers, or when the seam norm isn't fused.

On those layers, decode steps of 17-48 rows now run on plain vLLM ops instead of mono, which is a perf regression compared with `--monokernel` alone. It may be part of why DSpark at c64 only reaches parity.

Could the limit be decided per layer (keep 48 wherever the asm path doesn't take both halves)? Alternatively, `enabled()` could check the KV cache dtype and similar config-level conditions upfront, and the draft layers could keep mono's limit.

`weights()` makes a full repacked copy (`frag_w`) of every attention GEMV weight (`wqkv`, `wq_b`, `wo_a`, `wo_b`, `idx_wq_b`, plus `idx_wq_bq` on index layers) on every layer. vLLM keeps the original parameters for the fallback path. On top of that, `frag_w` expands the E8M0 scales 16× (`sc.unsqueeze(-1).expand(*sc.shape, 16).contiguous()` in `gemv8.py`). `AsmEngram`'s `_EngramSide` also keeps a resharded wkv (2·D rows instead of 5·D/4) next to the original.

All of this is allocated during the profile run, so it comes out of the KV cache budget. How many GiB per rank does this cost, and how does it change max KV blocks / max concurrency compared with `--monokernel` alone? Could the 16× scale expansion be avoided (index the scale by row block in-kernel)? Could the originals be freed or aliased where vLLM's fallback doesn't need them? Please state the memory cost in the PR description either way.

+norm's rrms, which ``attend(.., v3=True)`` folds into its score scale (and
+``q_rr`` applies for vLLM's attention on mixed steps). The y it returns is a
+placeholder: on consumer layers vLLM only passes it on to our attention.
+Index layers on v3 (``seam_v3(.., idx=True)``): y is y' = bf16(x1 ·
+attn_norm.w) without rstd; the indexer's weights_proj reads it and its wq_b
+reads front_v3's q x (no rrms), both off by a positive per-token factor that
+the top-k selection doesn't see; comp_tail(rs_part=) scales the compressor
+GEMM's rows by rstd itself. ``idx_q`` runs after ``front_v3`` as after ``front``.
+
+Activations between the pieces stay in the runner's scratch in gemv8's frag
+layout (sized for M = 256, allocated once; layers run one after another on a
+stream, so they share it). Weights are frag-shuffled copies (gemv8.frag_w),
+~40 MB per layer.

+import struct
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.asm.kernels import (
+    attn_dec1,
+    ffn_seam,
+    gemv8,
+    idx_logits,
+    idx_topk,
+    qkv_norm,
+)
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.asm.kernels.kmod import Kernel
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+
+H, MAX_M, HEADS, D = 5120, 256, 16, 512
+BF = torch.bfloat16
+ATTRS = {"wqkv": "fused_wqa_wkv", "wq_b": "wq_b", "wo_a": "wo_a", "wo_b": "wo_b"}
+GEMVS = {n: (gemv8.K1[n], a) for n, a in ATTRS.items()}
+GEMVS["idx_wq_b"] = (gemv8.IDX_WQ_B, "indexer.wq_b")
+
+
+def f32bits(v: float) -> int:
+    return struct.unpack("<I", struct.pack("<f", v))[0]
+
+
+gemv_mode = gemv8.k1_mode
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _translate_kernel(
+    out, lens, topk, topk_stride, req_of, valid, bt, bt_stride, bs, TOPK: tl.constexpr
+):
+    """Token t's top-k (local positions, -1 = none) → global slots at
+    out[t·TOPK ..] (-1 stays -1) and lens[t] = its non-negative count (0 for
+    an invalid token), as _compute_global_topk_ragged_indices_and_indptr_old."""
+    t = tl.program_id(0)
+    j = tl.arange(0, TOPK)
+    loc = tl.load(topk + t * topk_stride + j)
+    ok = loc >= 0
+    req = tl.load(req_of + t)
+    blk = tl.load(bt + req * bt_stride + loc // bs, mask=ok, other=0)
+    tl.store(out + t * TOPK + j, tl.where(ok, blk * bs + loc % bs, -1))
+    tl.store(lens + t, tl.where(tl.load(valid + t) != 0, tl.sum(ok.to(tl.int32), 0), 0))
+
+
+def attn_slog(m: int) -> int:
+    return 2 if m <= 64 else 1 if m <= 128 else 0
+
+
+class K1Runner:
+    def __init__(self, device=None, v3: bool = False):
+        self.dev = torch.device(device or "cuda")
+        self.v3 = v3
+        mk = lambda d, n=None: Kernel(
+            n or d["name"],
+            d["src"] if n is None else d["src"].replace(d["name"], n),
+            d["ka"],
+        )
+        self.k_seam = mk(ffn_seam.source_v2("k1_seam2"))
+        self.k_seam_eg = mk(ffn_seam.source_v2("k1_seam2_eg", post_stride=64))
+        self.k_fin = mk(ffn_seam.source_fin("k1_seam_fin", frag=True))
+        self.k_qkv = mk(qkv_norm.source())
+        self.k_attn = mk(attn_dec1.source("k1_attn", frag_out=True))
+        self.k_attn_fx = mk(
+            attn_dec1.source("k1_attn_fx", frag_out=True, tk_fixed=True)
+        )
+        self.k_lg: dict = {}
+        self.k_g = {}
+        for name, (cfg, _) in GEMVS.items():
+            for md in {gemv_mode(name, m) for m in (64, 128, 256)}:
+                self.k_g[name, md] = mk(gemv8.source(cfg, md), f"{cfg.name}_{md}")
+        if v3:
+            self.k_seam_q = mk(ffn_seam.source_v2("k1_seam2q", yq=True))
+            self.k_seam_eg_q = mk(
+                ffn_seam.source_v2("k1_seam2q_eg", post_stride=64, yq=True)
+            )
+            # index layers: + bf16 y' in x1's slot (the compressor GEMM and the
+            # indexer's weights_proj read it)
+            self.k_seam_fy = mk(ffn_seam.source_v2("k1_seam2fy", yq="fy"))
+            self.k_seam_eg_fy = mk(
+                ffn_seam.source_v2("k1_seam2fy_eg", post_stride=64, yq="fy")
+            )
+            d = gemv8.source(gemv8.WQKV32N, "k", mix_wave=True)
+            self.k_wqkv_mx, self.mx_block = mk(d), d["block"]
+            d = gemv8.source(gemv8.WQ_B, "k", kv_wave="rstd", kv_bar=True)
+            self.k_wqb_kv, self.kv_block = mk(d), d["block"]
+            # index layers: + the indexer's wq_b with its q RoPE + MXFP4 as extra CTAs
+            # (mode k)
+            d = gemv8.source(
+                gemv8.WQ_B,
+                "k",
+                kv_wave="rstd",
+                kv_bar=True,
+                extra=(gemv8.IDX_WQ_BQ, "k"),
+            )
+            self.k_wqb_kv_x2, self.x2_grid = mk(d), d["grid"]
+            # A3 with rr / rstd and bf16 split partials; speculative slot ids at M ≤ 128
+            # (attn_spec)
+            self.k_attn3 = {
+                (sp, fx): mk(
+                    attn_dec1.source(
+                        f"k1_attn3{'_sp' * sp}{'_fx' * fx}",
+                        frag_out=True,
+                        rr_scale="rstd",
+                        spec=sp,
+                        part_bf16=True,
+                        tk_fixed=fx,
+                    )
+                )
+                for sp in (False, True)
+                for fx in (False, True)
+            }
+        self._scratch()
+
+    def _scratch(self):
+        d = self.dev
+        u8 = lambda n: torch.zeros(n, dtype=torch.uint8, device=d)
+        self.s = dict(
+            x1=torch.empty(MAX_M, H, dtype=BF, device=d),
+            partial=torch.zeros(MAX_M, ffn_seam.SLICES, 32, device=d),
+            yq=u8(MAX_M * H),
+            ys=u8(MAX_M * H // 32),
+            qr_kv=torch.empty(MAX_M, 1792, dtype=BF, device=d),
+            qrq=u8(MAX_M * 1280),
+            qrs=u8(MAX_M * 40),
+            q=torch.empty(MAX_M, HEADS * D, dtype=BF, device=d),
+            iq=torch.empty(MAX_M, 4096, dtype=BF, device=d),
+            o=u8(MAX_M * HEADS * D),
+            os=u8(MAX_M * HEADS * D // 32),
+            z=u8(MAX_M * 2048),
+            zs=u8(MAX_M * 64),
+            apart=torch.zeros(MAX_M, attn_dec1.PSTRIDE // 4, device=d),
+            acnt=torch.zeros(MAX_M * 5, dtype=torch.int32, device=d),
+            dummy=u8(64),
+            tk=torch.empty(MAX_M * attn_dec1.TK_STRIDE, dtype=torch.int32, device=d),
+            tk_lens=torch.empty(MAX_M, dtype=torch.int32, device=d),
+            eye=torch.eye(4, device=d).expand(MAX_M, 4, 4).contiguous(),
+        )
+        if self.v3:
+            self.s.update(
+                iqc=u8(MAX_M * 2048).view(MAX_M, 32, 64),
+                iqs=u8(MAX_M * 128).view(MAX_M, 128),
+                ss=torch.zeros(MAX_M * 40, device=d),
+                rstd=torch.zeros(MAX_M, device=d),
+                y3=torch.empty(MAX_M, H, dtype=BF, device=d),
+                part_wqkv32=torch.zeros(gemv8.WQKV32N.part_bytes() // 4, device=d),
+                cnt_wqkv32=torch.zeros(gemv8.WQKV32N.NGP, dtype=torch.int32, device=d),
+            )
+            self._mix: tuple | None = None
+        for name, (cfg, _) in GEMVS.items():
+            self.s["part_" + name] = torch.zeros(
+                max(cfg.part_bytes() // 4, 1), device=d
+            )
+            self.s["cnt_" + name] = torch.zeros(cfg.NGP, dtype=torch.int32, device=d)
+
+    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- weights
+
+    def weights(self, layer, seam_only: bool = False, v3: bool = False) -> dict:
+        """Kernel-ready tensors of one DSv4.1 decoder layer's attention half
+        (+ the indexer's wq_b on index layers); seam_only: the seam's alone;
+        v3: wqkv for WQKV32N (instead of WQKV16's) and q_norm.weight in bf16."""
+        attn = layer.attn
+        w = dict(
+            fn_hl=ffn_seam.fn_hl(layer.hc_attn_fn.float()),
+            scale=layer.hc_attn_scale.float().contiguous(),
+            base=layer.hc_attn_base.float().contiguous(),
+            norm_w=layer.attn_norm.weight.to(BF).contiguous(),
+            rms_eps=f32bits(float(layer.rms_norm_eps)),
+            hc_eps=f32bits(float(layer.hc_eps)),
+            post_alpha=f32bits(float(layer.hc_post_alpha)),
+            norm_eps=f32bits(float(layer.attn_norm.variance_epsilon)),

+            kvw=attn.kv_norm.weight.data.contiguous(),

In the description, gsm8k is only compared to the out-of-tree plugin, not to the `--monokernel`-alone baseline on the same node. The c128 numbers (90.1 / 89.8 %) also look a bit lower than c16.

Could you add the baseline gsm8k (and ideally a longer-generation eval such as GPQA or AIME, where accumulated error shows up more) next to these runs, to back the 'No accuracy change' claim? Also, is MXFP8 on the wire required for the speedup? Was a bf16 wire measured? `_tool` takes the first `clang` / `ld.lld` on `PATH` before the ROCm LLVM. A host clang without the AMDGPU target (or an old one without gfx950 / MXFP instructions) passes `toolchain_missing()`, so `enabled()` turns the path on. The kernels then fail to assemble in `install()` during the first forward, which crashes the server instead of logging "asm decode off".

Suggestions:

- Prefer the ROCm LLVM (`/opt/rocm/llvm/bin`, or the ROCm SDK path) over `PATH`.
- Validate the toolchain in `toolchain_missing()` by assembling a trivial gfx950 snippet once.
- Or catch the build failure in `install()` and fall back (which must happen on every rank consistently).

The glob `/usr/local/lib/python3*/dist-packages/...` also misses venv / site-packages installs. Could it use `sysconfig` / the `_rocm_sdk_devel` module path instead?

+Kernels are generated per process at first use (some depend on the TP rank or the model's max length), assembled
+with clang and linked with ld.lld into code objects cached by source hash under $VLLM_CACHE_ROOT/dsv41_asm.
+vLLM's TP workers build the same kernels at once: every build writes per-process files and renames atomically,
+and the runner construction is serialised with ``build_lock()`` so one rank builds and the others hit the cache."""

+import contextlib
+import ctypes
+import fcntl
+import glob
+import hashlib
+import os
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+
+import vllm.envs as envs
+
+
+def cache_dir() -> str:
+    d = os.path.join(envs.VLLM_CACHE_ROOT, "dsv41_asm")
+    os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
+    return d
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def build_lock():
+    """Cross-process lock around kernel builds (vLLM's TP ranks build the same kernels at once)."""
+    with open(os.path.join(cache_dir(), ".build.lock"), "w") as lk:
+        fcntl.flock(lk, fcntl.LOCK_EX)

+    if p:

+    # the pip ROCm SDK (vLLM's ROCm images), then a system ROCm
+    for c in glob.glob(

+    ) + glob.glob(f"/opt/rocm*/llvm/bin/{name}"):

+
+

+
+

+    if not _tools:

Should this go through the shared specialized-decode abstraction instead of a second ad-hoc hook set? The RFC (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60904) proposes:

- code under `vllm/models/<model>/<vendor>/specialized_decode/`;
- one `plan()` per step that picks the specialized path or vLLM's forward.

#61311 (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61311) adds `DecodeSpec` / `SpecializedDecode` in `vllm/models/common/specialized_decode/` and refactors exactly this DSv4.1 gfx950 mono path onto it.

Here `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer` instead gets a second per-layer object (`self.asm` next to `self.mono`), a `_pre` wrapper, and per-call `x is state[...]` identity checks at the seam / attn / ffn sites. Each hook then decides independently whether to take the step. With mono (≤16 rows) and asm (17-256 rows) both present, wouldn't a single per-step plan that selects the row-range backend keep `model.py` smaller, and avoid conflicting with #61311 when either lands first?

How does this Engram side chain relate to two open DSv4.1 ROCm PRs that rework the same chain?

- #63326 (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63326) runs the Engram WKV chain on a side stream and replaces the gathers with IPC pushes. It adds `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/engram_ahead.py` and touches `common/engram.py` and `amd/model.py`.
- #63367 (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63367) shards the Engram gate so ranks gather only the value slice.

`_EngramSide` combines both ideas (wkv resharded to [key copy r | value], a split IPC push / wait for the rows, a 16 B gate all-gather) as a subclass that overrides `_start_prefetch` / `forward`. Should these converge on one implementation in `common/engram.py` / `amd/engram.py`, so the asm path only adds the seam-side gate · value? Otherwise, whichever lands later has to rebase over two incompatible `Engram` overrides.
