+    MXFP8 quant of the rank's own rows (vLLM's op; the 32-blocks sit inside the
+    256-wide hash columns, so the codes are those of vLLM's quant of the
+    gathered rows), all-gather of [codes | scales], GEMM into a persistent
+    buffer. The rows all-gather is split: the main stream pushes (at layer 0's
+    attention eager break, when the lookups are long done), the prefetch stream

+        )

+        index_q: torch.Tensor | None,
+        index_q_scale: torch.Tensor | None,
+        index_weights: torch.Tensor | None,
+        q: torch.Tensor,
+        kv: torch.Tensor,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        out: torch.Tensor,
+    ) -> None:
+        """The attention's eager break (``_sparse_indexer_and_attn``): the
+        indexer top-k and the sparse attention, ours where they apply."""
+        if self.flush_engram:
+            from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.asm.engram import eg_flush
+
+            eg_flush(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+        if attn.indexer is not None and index_q is not None:
+            assert index_weights is not None
+            q_quant = (index_q, index_q_scale) if index_q_scale is not None else index_q
+            args = (hidden_states, q_quant, None, index_weights)
+            if self.idx_topk_fn is not None:
+                self.idx_topk_fn(*args)
+            else:
+                attn.indexer.indexer_op(*args)
+            if self.tk_hook is not None:
+                self.tk_hook()
+        if self.mqa_fn is not None:
+            self.mqa_fn(q, kv, positions, out)
+        else:
+            attn.forward_mqa(q, kv, positions, out)
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- K2: the FFN half
+
+_k2: dict = {"runner": None, "seen": set()}
+
+
+def _k2_install(h: AsmDecodeLayer, layer, lo: int, hi: int) -> None:
+    """The FFN seam call (``mhc_pre_delayed`` with ``hc_ffn_fn``) runs K2 for
+    lo <= M <= hi and returns a token in the x slot; ``ffn`` then runs the
+    combine + all-reduce #2 on it, as vLLM's MoE runner reduces routed +
+    shared."""
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.asm.k2_runner import K2Runner, raw_from_layer
+
+    _comb_setup()
+    if not layer.fuse_seam_norm:
+        _log("K2 off for a layer: the seam doesn't fuse the norm")
+        return
+    ffn = layer.ffn
+    if ffn.gate.weight.shape[0] != E:
+        # DSpark's draft layers (128 experts, top 3) stay on vLLM
+        _log(
+            f"K2 off for layer {layer.attn.layer_id}: "
+            f"{ffn.gate.weight.shape[0]} experts"
+        )
+        return
+    if (
+        ffn.shared_experts is None
+        or ffn.gate.tid2eid is not None
+        or ffn.n_activated_experts != 6
+        or ffn.routed_scaling_factor != 1.5
+        or ffn.swiglu_limit != 10.0
+        or ffn.scoring_func != "sqrtsoftplus"
+        or not ffn.renormalize
+    ):
+        _log(f"K2 off for layer {layer.attn.layer_id}: MoE routing")
+        return
+    assert not torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing(), (
+        "K2 must be set up outside graph capture"
+    )
+    if _k2["runner"] is None:
+        from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.asm.kernels.build import build_lock
+
+        with build_lock():
+            _k2["runner"] = K2Runner("chain", v3=True)
+    run = _k2["runner"]
+    wt = run.weights(raw_from_layer(layer))
+    state: dict = {"part": None}
+
+    def seam_forward(*args, **kw):
+        # the FFN seam call: 9 positional (residual, hc_ffn_fn, ...
+        # sinkhorn_repeat), the rest by keyword
+        residual: Any = args[0]
+        m = residual.shape[0]
+        mixes: list[Any] = [
+            kw.get(k)
+            for k in ("sublayer_out", "pre_mix", "post_layer_mix", "comb_res_mix")
+        ]
+        sub, pre_mix, post_mix, res_mix = mixes
+        if (
+            len(args) != 9
+            or args[1] is not layer.hc_ffn_fn
+            or kw.get("x") is not None
+            or kw.get("norm_weight") is None
+            or any(t is None for t in (sub, pre_mix, post_mix, res_mix))
+            or residual.dim() != 3
+            or not lo <= m <= hi
+        ):
+            return None
+        if m not in _k2["seen"]:
+            _k2["seen"].add(m)
+            _log(f"K2 at M = {m}")
+        part, r_new, post, comb, pre = run(
+            wt,
+            sub.contiguous(),
+            residual.contiguous(),
+            post_mix.contiguous(),
+            res_mix.contiguous(),
+            pre_mix.contiguous(),
+            fold=True,
+        )
+        # unwritten: a token for ffn_forward
+        state["part"] = part
+        state["comb_in"] = run.comb_in
+        return r_new, post, comb, part, pre
+
+    def ffn_forward(x):
+        if state["part"] is not None and x is state["part"]:
+            state["part"] = None
+            return _comb["car"](*state.pop("comb_in"), x.shape[0], WIRE)
+        return None
+
+    h.seams.insert(0, seam_forward)
+    h.ffn_fn = ffn_forward
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- K1: the attention
+# half
+
+_k1: dict = {"runner": None, "seen": set(), "logged": set()}
+
+
+def _log_once(key, msg: str) -> None:
+    if key not in _k1["logged"]:
+        _k1["logged"].add(key)
+        _log(msg)
+
+
+def _k1_runner():
+    """The process's one K1Runner (built on first use, under the build lock)."""
+    if _k1["runner"] is None:
+        from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.asm.k1_runner import K1Runner
+        from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.asm.kernels.build import build_lock
+
+        with build_lock():
+            _k1["runner"] = K1Runner(v3=True)
+    return _k1["runner"]
+
+
+def _idx_topk_install(h: AsmDecodeLayer, attn, run, metadata) -> None:
+    """On pure decode steps the indexer op runs ours: logits + top-512 in one
+    launch (decode rows only; graph-padded rows get none), writing vLLM's top-k
+    buffer and the runner's fixed-stride lists. Rows up to 4 · 512 · 18
+    compressed positions take one CTA per row; dense layers up to 16 · 16384
+    the wide split kernels; the candidate source (ratio 1) up to 32 · 16384 the
+    wide kernels with its block scores and top-2048 blocks; the candidate
+    consumers the gather mode over the row's candidate blocks. Wider rows (1M
+    context) keep vLLM's op, as do prefill / mixed steps."""
+    from vllm.v1.attention.ops.rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer import _layer
+
+    op = attn.indexer.indexer_op

This override re-decorates the method and calls `super()._sparse_indexer_and_attn.__wrapped__`. `AsmDecodeLayer.sparse_indexer_and_attn` then re-implements the same body as the base: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/20d7dd9ac15292357ed474856cf268af9dd730ba/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py#L737-L760 This leaves two copies to keep in sync, and the override depends on the base keeping exactly one `functools.wraps` decorator.

The asm layer only needs to swap three things: `indexer_op`, `forward_mqa`, and a hook after the top-k (plus the Engram flush on layer 0). Would it be simpler to inject those as hooks (e.g. the asm layer sets `self.asm_indexer_op` / `self.asm_forward_mqa` callables that the existing body uses when set)? Then neither the decorator nor the base body would need duplicating.

Could these share one small utility (e.g. under `vllm/platforms/rocm` or `vllm/utils`) so future asm kernels don't add a third copy? A follow-up would also be fine, but the PR could at least reuse the existing helpers where their signatures match.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+# mypy: ignore-errors
+# ruff: noqa: E501  (one asm instruction or template line per source line)
+"""Assemble and link the generated gfx950 kernels, and reach HIP through ctypes.
+
+Kernels are generated per process at first use (some depend on the TP rank or the model's max length), assembled
+with clang and linked with ld.lld into code objects cached by source hash under $VLLM_CACHE_ROOT/dsv41_asm.
+vLLM's TP workers build the same kernels at once: every build writes per-process files and renames atomically,
+and the runner construction is serialised with ``build_lock()`` so one rank builds and the others hit the cache."""
+
+import contextlib
+import ctypes
+import fcntl
+import glob
+import hashlib
+import os
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+
+import vllm.envs as envs
+
+
+def cache_dir() -> str:
+    d = os.path.join(envs.VLLM_CACHE_ROOT, "dsv41_asm")
+    os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
+    return d
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def build_lock():
+    """Cross-process lock around kernel builds (vLLM's TP ranks build the same kernels at once)."""
+    with open(os.path.join(cache_dir(), ".build.lock"), "w") as lk:
+        fcntl.flock(lk, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
+        try:
+            yield
+        finally:
+            fcntl.flock(lk, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
+
+
+def _tool(name: str) -> str | None:
+    p = shutil.which(name)
+    if p:
+        return p
+    # the pip ROCm SDK (vLLM's ROCm images), then a system ROCm
+    for c in glob.glob(
+        f"/usr/local/lib/python3*/dist-packages/_rocm_sdk_devel/lib/llvm/bin/{name}"
+    ) + glob.glob(f"/opt/rocm*/llvm/bin/{name}"):
+        return c
+    return None
+
+
+_tools: dict = {}
+
+
+def toolchain_missing() -> str | None:
+    """None if clang and ld.lld (LLVM with the AMDGPU target) are found, else what is missing."""
+    if not _tools:
+        _tools.update(clang=_tool("clang"), lld=_tool("ld.lld"))
+    missing = [k for k, v in _tools.items() if v is None]
+    return " and ".join(missing) or None
+
+
+def build(src: str, name: str) -> bytes:
+    """Assemble + link ``src`` → code object bytes, cached by source hash."""
+    if toolchain_missing():
+        raise FileNotFoundError(
+            f"building the asm decode kernels needs {toolchain_missing()}"
+        )
+    h = hashlib.sha1(src.encode()).hexdigest()[:12]
+    base = os.path.join(cache_dir(), f"{name}-{h}")
+    co = base + ".co"
+    if not os.path.exists(co):
+        # per-process files, then an atomic rename (several ranks may build the same new kernel at once)
+        tmp = f"{base}.{os.getpid()}"
+        with open(tmp + ".s", "w") as f:
+            f.write(src)
+        r = subprocess.run(
+            [
+                _tools["clang"],
+                "-x",
+                "assembler",
+                "-target",
+                "amdgcn-amd-amdhsa",
+                "-mcpu=gfx950",
+                "-c",
+                tmp + ".s",
+                "-o",
+                tmp + ".o",
+            ],
+            capture_output=True,
+            text=True,
+        )
+        if r.returncode:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"assemble failed ({tmp}.s):\n" + "\n".join(r.stderr.splitlines()[:12])
+            )
+        r = subprocess.run(
+            [_tools["lld"], "-shared", tmp + ".o", "-o", tmp + ".co"],
+            capture_output=True,
+            text=True,
+        )
+        if r.returncode:
+            raise RuntimeError(f"link failed:\n{r.stderr}")
+        os.remove(tmp + ".s")
+        os.remove(tmp + ".o")
+        os.replace(tmp + ".co", co)
+    with open(co, "rb") as f:
+        return f.read()
+
+
+_hip = None
+
+
+def hip():
+    """The HIP runtime torch loaded (found in the process's maps, so it is the same library instance)."""
+    global _hip
+    if _hip is None:
+        import torch
+
+        torch.zeros(1, device="cuda")  # make torch load and initialise the runtime
+        lib = None
+        with open("/proc/self/maps") as f:
+            for line in f:
+                if "libamdhip64.so" in line:
+                    lib = line.split()[-1]
+                    break
+        _hip = ctypes.CDLL(lib or "libamdhip64.so")
+        _hip.hipModuleLaunchKernel.argtypes = (
+            [ctypes.c_void_p]
+            + [ctypes.c_uint] * 7
+            + [ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p]
+        )
+        _hip.hipGetErrorString.restype = ctypes.c_char_p
+    return _hip
+
+
+def _check(err: int, what: str) -> None:
+    if err:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"{what}: hip error {err} {hip().hipGetErrorString(err).decode()}"
+        )

> My main (human) comment/question is why this PR is not part of #60904, i.e. using `--monokernel` / specialized decode infra. Of course, this PR does not implement just 1/2 kernels, but it seems to fit still?
> 
> I am also curious as to:
> 
> * Why can't this work be broken down in AITER / vLLM to improve ALL MOE/linear/attention backends ? Not only DS-v4.1 ? Surely some of the work done here is not specific to DS-V4.1 ?
> * what is the benefit from generating assembly kernels at first forward call as compared to have them shipped e.g. as part of AITER, which AFAIK is already something being done.
> * Why would this be preferred to have in vLLM shipped as python, rather than `.s`/`.co` assembly? I guess one generator for different variants?
> * Does assembly over FlyDSL allow anything that a DSL like FlyDSL does not enable?
> 
> For reference: https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/blob/0f61f2b95d0b4c054a1b5bb644543e74a3f088b3/hsa/gfx950/mla/mla_a16w16_qh16_m16x4_n16x1_coex0_mask1.co (note: aiter ships binary without source.)


There are some discrepancies the test placement from the rfc, it was copied from another PR. The actual code itself is under the monoekernel path. pyproject.toml was changed because precommit hooks flagged offen as a typo but that's a keyword in AMD assembly, and we can hardly change that. The tests seem to be the only part not following the rfc.

The reason this is a single blob is because it has been optimized as a single blob, as in kernel boundaries have been chosen to be bespoke to DSv4.1 with no limitations in fusions and sizes are hardcoded, the kernels simply do not work over M 256 and exact DSv4.1 sizes. We could separate them and look for sharing but nowadays that actually takes more time and effort than just doing the bespoke part per model.

The reason the kernels are shipped like this is to both have generators and allow just python files in a PR. We could pregen them and ship even fully assembled versions but the benefits are questionable. And the kernels are for vLLM only. Shipping single model vLLM only kernels in AITER would not bring much benefit, and just introduce undue delay in shipping to users as one first needs to wait for AITER PR, then pinning new AITER to vLLM and then the final vLLM PR.

Assembly over FlyDSL allows more precise instruction scheduling. With FlyDSL one has to figure out how to get the FlyDSL generate the instructions you want, with direct assembly one can just put in what has been found to be efficient.

This sort of development does not make sense if there are humans in the loop. These are there result of agentic optimization loops bespoke for that single problem, so they are essentially black boxes where we have verified the numerical results of the kernels both individually and as part of real serving.

I would like to comment that I do not necessarily want this kind of PR to land. But we need infrastructure in vLLM side to enable us to ship custom kernel pipelines like this. As an example sglang has solved this by having a stable-ish plugin API and separate repo for the custom implementations.

Future will only bring more of these, we need to be able to ship them while keeping vLLM itself a great framework to run inference with. After all the inference kernels and model impls themselves are nowhere near all that vLLM has to offer.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Agent review, feel free to ignore irrelevant items, apologize if any!

With this PR, a decoder layer on a 17–256-row decode step runs as a chain of roughly 10–15 launches:

 1. `k1_seam2q` (`k1_seam2fy` on index layers, `*_eg` after an Engram layer): attention seam, i.e. mHC post-mix of the previous FFN + pre-mix, Σx² partials, MXFP8 of x · attn_norm.w.
 2. `gemv_wqkv32n`: wqkv GEMV (q / kv rows), plus a wave finishing the seam's mixes (post / comb / pre, rstd).
 3. `wq_b` GEMV (`gemv8`, kv wave): wq_b + q RoPE, and the kv norm + RoPE + SWA cache insert in the same launch.
     - index layers: the `_x2` variant, which also runs the indexer's wq_b + q RoPE + MXFP4 quant as extra CTAs;
     - index layers, on aux streams in parallel: `comp_gemm` + `comp_tail` (Triton: compressor GEMM, pooling / norm, compressed KV insert, indexer K store) and vLLM's `weights_proj`.
 4. Index layers only, in the attention eager break: indexer logits + top-512, one of:
     - `idx_logits` (fused logits + top-512, one CTA per row), for short rows;
     - the wide split-logits kernel + its merge kernel, plus the top-2048 candidate-block selector on the candidate-source layer;
     - the gather-mode kernel, on candidate-consumer layers;
     - `_translate_kernel` (Triton) when vLLM's top-k ran instead (wider rows).
 5. `k1_attn3`: sparse attention (SWA + compressed top-k), in the attention eager break.
 6. `wo_a` GEMV (`gemv8`, k or t mode).
 7. `wob_ar`: wo_b GEMV with all-reduce #1 folded in (fp8 wire).
 8. `ffn_seam2_ug`: FFN seam (mHC post-mix of the attention + pre-mix, Σx² partials, MXFP8 + bf16 of x · ffn_norm.w).
 9. `ffn_rt_sgu`, two bodies merged into one launch (`multi.py`):
     - router logits partials (bf16 MFMA);
     - shared-expert gate_up partials (fp8 MFMA).
 10. `ffn_p3v3`: one CTA per token:
     - rstd, router finish (sqrt-softplus + bias, top-6, renormalise × 1.5);
     - shared-expert finish (SwiGLU, MXFP8);
     - a 5th wave finishing the FFN seam's mixes.
 11. `ffn_prep_sdn`, two bodies merged into one launch:
     - MoE prep (sort tokens by expert, per-expert counts / cost split);
     - shared-expert down GEMV.
 12. `moe_ug1`: routed-expert stage 1 (MXFP4 gate_up + SwiGLU).
 13. `moe_down1_table`: routed-expert stage 2 (MXFP4 down).
 14. `comb_ar`: MoE combine (weighted routed + shared) with all-reduce #2 folded in (fp8 wire).

That is 13 launches on a non-index layer, and 14–16 on an index layer (plus the two Triton compressor launches on aux streams). Dense / ratio-0 layers (e.g. layer 0) only take the K2 half (launches 8–14) and keep vLLM's attention. On Engram layers, the gate all-gather and the rows push / wait (`eg_ag`) are added.

My main (human) comment/question is why this PR is not part of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60904, i.e. using `--monokernel` / specialized decode infra. Of course, this PR does not implement just 1/2 kernels, but it seems to fit still? Don't we already have the infrastructure to allow multiple different specialized decode paths? I think it would be already the case with gfx950, gfx942 targets, etc.

I am also curious as to:
- Why can't this work be broken down in AITER / vLLM to improve ALL MOE/linear/attention backends ? Not only DS-v4.1 ? Surely some of the work done here is not specific to DS-V4.1 ?
- what is the benefit from generating assembly kernels at first forward call as compared to have them shipped e.g. as part of AITER, which AFAIK is already something being done.
- Why would this be preferred to have in vLLM shipped as python, rather than `.s`/`.co` assembly? I guess one generator for different variants?
- Does assembly over FlyDSL allow anything that a DSL like FlyDSL does not enable?

For reference: https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/blob/0f61f2b95d0b4c054a1b5bb644543e74a3f088b3/hsa/gfx950/mla/mla_a16w16_qh16_m16x4_n16x1_coex0_mask1.co (note: aiter ships binary without source.)
